children.translated_text: He states the fivefold motion of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) with the words beginning "water-going."

children.text: jalarūpeṇa dravatvena jalagaḥ jalena saha gamanaśīlaḥ bhavet rasasya cūrṇaprāyo 'tisūkṣmāṃśa iti bhāvaḥ tvaritaḥ cañcalaḥ cāñcalyādityarthaḥ haṃsagaḥ haṃsavad gamanaśīlaḥ bhavet malarūpeṇa malavattvāt malagaḥ malena saha miśritaḥ doṣasaṃśliṣṭaḥ bhavet sadhūmaḥ vahnidṛṣṭatvāt dhūmagaḥ dhūmena saha gamanaśīlaḥ uḍḍayanasvabhāvaḥ bhavet anyā aparā pañcamītyarthaḥ daivī adṛśyarūpā jīvasya rasasya gatiḥ gamanam astīti śeṣaḥ tayā gatyā aṇḍāt deharūpakośāt jīvaḥ ātmā iva niṣkramet rasa iti bhāvaḥ kena pathā dehāt jīvo nirgacchati tat yathā na dṛśyate tathā pāradasya pañcamī gatirapi na jñātum śakyate ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Water-going" means that, in the form of water, because of its fluidity, it goes together with water; the sense is that <s>rasa</s> has extremely minute particles, almost like powder. "Swift" means restless, that is, because of its instability. "Swan-going" means that it moves like a swan. Because it has the form of impurity, like impurity, it is "impurity-going," mixed with impurity and connected with defects. Being smoky, because it is seen in fire, it is "smoke-going," moving together with smoke and having the nature of flying upward. "Another" means a further, fifth motion. There is a divine, invisible motion of living <s>rasa</s>; this is to be supplied. By that motion, <s>rasa</s> departs like a living self from the egg, that is, from the body-like sheath. The meaning is: just as the path by which the soul leaves the body is not seen, so too the fifth motion of mercury cannot be known.

children.text: pūrvaśloke jīvagatiśabdena rasagatiriti pradarśitaṃ jīvaśabdasya rasārthatve hetumāha sa iti ||
children.translated_text: In the preceding verse it was shown by the word "motion of the living being" that the motion meant is that of <s>rasa</s>. Now he gives the reason why the word "living being" has the sense of <s>rasa</s>, with the words beginning "it."

children.text: saḥ rasaḥ tān jīvān jīvayet jarāmaraṇādivināśanadvārā dīrghajīvanaṃ pradāpayet tena hetunā rasaḥ jīvaḥ jīvayatīti vyutpattyā jīvanadāyakaḥ smṛtaḥ kathitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>rasa</s> makes those living beings live: through the removal of old age, death, and so forth, it grants long life. For that reason <s>rasa</s> is remembered, or described, as <s>jīva</s>, the giver of life, by the derivation "it makes live."
It may be <s>matsyākṣikā</s>, <s>hilamocikā</s>, or <s>gaṇḍadūrvā</s>.
He explains the procedure for <s>dhānyābhra</s> with the words beginning "powdered mica."

children.text: cūrṇābhra abhracūrṇaṃ śālisaṃyuktam adyāpyatra śāliparimāṇaṃ noktaṃ tathāpi tantrāntarānusaraṇāt pādamitaśālidhānyasahitaṃ boddhavyaṃ tathā ca rasendrasārasaṃgrahe
children.translated_text: "Powdered mica" means mica powder mixed with rice. Although the amount of rice is not stated here, still, following another tantra, it should be understood as combined with one quarter measure of rice grain. Thus, in the <s>Rasendrasārasaṃgraha</s>:
"Mica, combined with a quarter part of rice, inside a blanket,
should be placed in water for three nights; when it is soaked, one should grind it firmly.
What passes through the blanket, smooth and free of sand,
that is called <s>dhānyābhra</s>, for the successful incineration of mica."
Thus.
"Issued out" means gone out.

children.text: abhraṃ cūrṇitaṃ kṛtvā pādāṃśaśālidhānyena saha sthūlavastre baddhvā kāñjike tāvanmardanīyaṃ yāvad vastracchidrāt ślakṣṇaṃ vālukārahitaṃ sat niryāti taddhānyābhraṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: After making mica into powder, binding it in a coarse cloth together with a quarter part of rice grain, it should be ground in sour gruel until, being smooth and free of sand, it comes out through the holes of the cloth. That is remembered as <s>dhānyābhra</s>.
"Thrown in" means cast in.
"With an iron pestle" means with a pestle made of iron.

children.text: vallaḥ dviguñjā guñjātrayam iti līlāvatī sārdhaguñjeti rājanighaṇṭuḥ ||
children.translated_text: A <s>valla</s> is two <s>guñjā</s>s; according to the <s>Līlāvatī</s> it is three <s>guñjā</s>s, and according to the <s>Rājanighaṇṭu</s> it is one and a half <s>guñjā</s>s.
He states the variety of <s>vimala</s> with the words beginning "vimala."
<s>Vimala</s> is a particular kind of <s>mākṣika</s>.
"By each respective luster" means by the shine of gold and the others.
In the <s>Paryāyamuktāvalī</s>, by the word <s>vimala</s>, silver <s>mākṣika</s> is understood.
<s>Kāṅkṣī</s> is the clay of <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>.

children.text: tatrādau svarṇādibhya utpattibhedena trividhasya gomūtragandhinaḥ tasya lakṣaṇādikamāha svarṇeti ||
children.translated_text: There, first, he states the characteristics and other details of that threefold substance, smelling of cow urine, according to its origin from gold and the other metals, with the words beginning "golden."

children.text: tantrāntare tu utpattibhedena bhinnasya tasya cāturvidhyamuktaṃ yathā carake
children.translated_text: But in another tantra, its fourfoldness, differing according to origin, is stated, as in <s>Caraka</s>:
"Not excessively hot or cold, it arises from four metals:
from gold, then from silver, from copper, and better even from black iron."
Thus.

children.text: atra tu āyasaṃ noktaṃ tallakṣaṇamapi tatraiva draṣṭavyaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Here iron is not mentioned. Its characteristics too are to be seen in that same source, as follows:
"That which resembles <s>guggulu</s>, is bitter and joined with salt,

children.text: vipāke kaṭu śītaṃ ca sarvaśreṣṭhaṃ tadāyasaṃ ||
children.translated_text: pungent in digestion and cold: that iron-born kind is the best of all.
All of them smell of cow urine and are suitable for all operations;
but in rejuvenating applications the last is especially distinguished."
Thus.

children.text: atra haimaśilājatuno paramarasāyanatvenoktatvād āyasasyāpi mukhyataḥ rasāyanaguṇatvena ekakāryakatvād āyasaṃ pṛthaṅnoktamiti mantavyam ||
children.translated_text: Here, because golden <s>śilājatu</s> has been stated to be the supreme rejuvenative, and because the iron-born kind also has essentially the same function by virtue of its rejuvenating quality, it should be understood that the iron-born type has not been stated separately.
<s>Capala</s> is zinc; in common speech it is called <s>dasta</s>.

children.text: rasakasya dvaividhyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cāha rasaka iti ||
children.translated_text: He states the twofold division and characteristic of <s>rasaka</s> with the words beginning "rasaka."
<s>Rasaka</s> is a particular substance produced from <s>kharparī</s> and <s>tuttha</s>. As is said in the <s>Bhāvaprakāśa</s>:

children.text: kharparītutthakaṃ tutthād anyat tad rasakaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: "What is produced from <s>kharparī</s> and <s>tuttha</s>, but is different from <s>tuttha</s>, is remembered as <s>rasaka</s>;

children.text: ye guṇāstutthake proktāste guṇāḥ rasake smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the qualities stated for <s>tuttha</s> are remembered as the qualities of <s>rasaka</s>."
Thus.
"With leaves" means possessing leaf-like plates; the sense is that it is like bamboo-leaf orpiment.
"In a <s>kharpara</s>" means in an earthen bowl.
He states another opinion with the words beginning "in a pot."
In the phrase "one should kindle," the word "fire" is to be supplied.
"With forest-dung" means with forest cow-dung cakes.
"With dung cakes" means with dried balls of domestic cow dung.
This explains "from the application."

children.text: phullatuvarīlepena tāmraṃ lauhāṃśam ujhati tāmre yaḥ lauhāṃśaḥ vidyate sa nirgacchatītyarthaḥ tāmraṃ lauhavat kāṭhinyaṃ gacchatītyartho vā ||
children.translated_text: By an application of blossomed <s>tuvarī</s>, copper casts off its iron element: the meaning is that the iron element which exists in copper comes out. Or the meaning is that copper becomes hard like iron.
"Having the form of the top of an anthill" means marked by many raised and depressed peaks like an anthill.
<s>Gaurīpāṣāṇa</s> is a white stone, called <s>phulkhaḍi</s> in common speech.
<s>Vahnijāra</s>, known by its own name, is a particular medicine produced in the western ocean.
<s>Mṛddāraśṛṅga</s> is a particular mountain mineral produced from lead.
"Rich in moonlight" means possessing sparkle, that is, having many bright particles like mica with moonlike spots.

children.text: gaurīpāṣāṇasya paryāyān varṇabhedena traividhyaṃ cāha gaurīti ||
children.translated_text: He states the synonyms of <s>gaurīpāṣāṇa</s> and its threefold division according to difference in color with the words beginning "gaurī."
"Yellow," "misshapen," and "struck powder" are these three synonyms.
"Earlier," and so on.

children.text: pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ haridrābhagaurīpāṣāṇāt śaṅkhābhaḥ śaṅkhābhapāṣāṇāt sphaṭikābhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of the preceding ones, the earlier is superior: the one resembling conch is superior to <s>haridrābha gaurīpāṣāṇa</s>, and the one resembling crystal is superior to the stone resembling conch.
He states the essential characteristic of <s>girisindūra</s> with the word beginning "great."
A particular red-colored rasa-substance, dried after issuing from between two small stones lying inside great mountains such as the Himalaya, is known as <s>girisindūra</s>.
He states the characteristic and place of origin of <s>mṛddāraśṛṅga</s> with the word beginning "with leaves."
It is marked by layers, like bamboo-leaf orpiment.

children.text: mṛddāraśṛṅgasya paryāyādikaṃ nighaṇṭvādau anyatra vā kutrāpi granthe na paridṛśyate paraṃ tu asmaddeśe yanmudrāśaṅkha iti nāmnā prasiddhaṃ paścimadeśe tat murdārśiṅ iti nāmnā tatratyairabhidhīyate ato manye mṛddāraśṛṅgakaṃ mudrāśaṅkha eva iti ||
children.translated_text: The synonyms and other details of <s>mṛddāraśṛṅga</s> are not seen in nighaṇṭus or in any other treatise anywhere. But in our region what is famous by the name <s>mudrāśaṅkha</s> is called <s>murdārśiṅ</s> by the people there in the western country; therefore I think that <s>mṛddāraśṛṅga</s> is just <s>mudrāśaṅkha</s>.

children.text: toyaprabhaṃ jalābhaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati tatra dūrato jalabhramotpādakam ityarthaḥ yadvā jalavat taralacchāyaṃ lāvaṇyaviśiṣṭam iti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: "Having the appearance of water" means water-like; the sense is that, where it is, it produces from afar the mistaken impression of water. Or, it means possessing a fluid luster like water, that is, endowed with beauty.

children.text: nirjalaṃ nirjaḍaṃ ḍalayor aikyāt aśiśiramityarthaḥ uṣṇamiti yāvad yadvā vicchāyaṃ dṛśyate ca lāvaṇye jalaśabdopacāraḥ muktāphalasya taralacchāyā eva lāvaṇyaśabdabodhikā yaduktaṃ
children.translated_text: "Without water" means without coldness, since ḍa and ja are equivalent; the sense is "not cold," that is, hot. Or else it is seen as lacking luster, and the word "water" is figuratively applied to beauty. In a pearl, it is precisely a fluid luster that conveys the word "beauty," as it has been said:
"As the fluidity of luster within pearls
appears in limbs, that is here called beauty."
Thus.
Here, by the word "water," the fluid luster found in a pearl is to be understood.
"Misshapen" means having an uneven body.
"Pale" means a color mixed of white and yellow.
"Grey" means a color mixed of white and black.

children.text: aṣṭaphalakam aṣṭadhāram astrādīnām agrabhāgavat sūkṣmāgram ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Eight-faceted" means having eight edges; the sense is that its tip is fine, like the front part of weapons and the like.

children.text: nirdalaṃ niṣpattram aśubhagomedasya sapaṭalatvād atra śubhagomedasya nirdalatvāvatāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: "Without leaves" means without plates. Since bad <s>gomedaka</s> has layers, here the leaflessness of good <s>gomedaka</s> is being introduced.
<s>Lakuca</s> is <s>ḍahuka</s>.
"The group of eight metals" means the eight metals, and that consists of gold, silver, copper, tin, lead, brass, magnetic iron, and sharp iron.
"By enemy-metal," that is, by an enemy of metal, means by orpiment.
<s>Prativāpa</s> is the sprinkling of another substance upon molten metal.
<s>Devadālī</s> is <s>hastighoṣaka</s>.
"Free from eruptions" means free from swellings like sores.
"Applied" means made into a paste, that is, ground.
He states another opinion with the word beginning "in a potsherd."
"With ash and powder" means with lead ash and borax powder; <s>pālikā</s> means a surrounding channel.

children.text: atrāyaṃ vidhiḥ nāgabhasmaṭaṅkaṇacūrṇe jalena piṣṭvā tatpiṇḍena mṛtkharparaṃ paritaḥ ālavālaṃ racayitvā tanmadhye samasīsacūrṇapiṣṭaraupyaṃ nikṣipya tāvat bhastrayā dhamet yāvat sīsakṣayo na bhavediti ||
children.translated_text: Here the procedure is this: after grinding lead ash and borax powder with water, one should make a surrounding channel all around an earthen potsherd with that lump. In its middle one should place silver ground with an equal amount of lead powder, and then blow with a bellows until the lead is not destroyed.

children.text: sadalaṃ sapattraṃ paṭalasaṃyutam iti yāvat dalaṃ jor iti loke iti bhāvamiśraḥ ||
children.translated_text: "With leaves" means having leaves, that is, joined with layers. <s>Bhāvamiśra</s> says that <s>dala</s> is <s>jor</s> in common speech.
<s>Amlaparṇī</s> is <s>cāṅgerī</s>.

children.text: pogaraṃ kuñcitālakavat taraṅgāyitaṃ tena unmuktaṃ tadrahitam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pogara</s> means wavy like curled hair; "freed from that" means devoid of it.

children.text: kharalakṣaṇe pogaronmuktam ityuktam ataḥ pogarasya paryāyādikam āha aṅgakṣayeti ||
children.translated_text: Since, in the characteristic of <s>khara</s>, it is said to be "free from <s>pogara</s>," he states the synonyms and other details of <s>pogara</s> with the word beginning "wasting of the body."

children.text: tritvaṃ cātra pogaram apekṣya bodhyaṃ tena aṅgakṣayā vaṅgaṃ pogaraṃ ca ityekārtham ||
children.translated_text: Here the threefoldness should be understood with reference to <s>pogara</s>; therefore <s>aṅgakṣayā</s>, tin, and <s>pogara</s> have one meaning.
He states the essential characteristic of <s>pogara</s> with the word beginning "hair."
"From iron" means on the body of iron.

children.text: atra saptamyarthe pañcamīti boddhavyam yat cikuraṃ bhaṅguraṃ kuñcitakuntalavadbhaṅgīviśeṣaḥ ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the fifth case should be understood in the sense of the seventh: the meaning is that <s>cikura</s> is brittle, a particular bend like curled hair.

children.text: sparśavedhi sparśamātreṇaiva vedhakārakaṃ rasendrasya vedhākhyasaṃskārasaṃpādakaṃ vā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Penetrating by touch" means causing penetration by mere touch, or accomplishing for <s>rasendra</s> the operation called penetration.
"Emptied" means caused to flow out.
<s>Triśūlī</s> means three small cakes, like a trident.

children.text: niḥśabdaṃ pattrībhūtamapi śabdarahitaṃ pattrībhūtaṃ raṅgāntaraṃ yathā saśabdaṃ bhavati tathā na ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Soundless" means that, even when made into leaf, it is without sound; the sense is that it does not become noisy the way another form of tin does when made into leaf.
<s>Bhāradvāja</s> means wild cotton.
<s>Nākulībīja</s> is the seed of <s>rāsnā</s> or the seed of <s>śālmalī</s>.

children.text: mahārājagiriḥ śākaviśeṣaḥ rājaśākam itiyāvat sa tu laghusthūlabhedena dvividhaḥ atra ca sthūlo grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahārājagiri</s> is a kind of vegetable, that is, <s>rājaśāka</s>. It is of two kinds, small and large; here the large one is to be taken.

children.text: atredaṃ kāryaṃ vakrākārāṃ cullīṃ kṛtvā tadupari ghaṭamekaṃ vakramukhaṃ kṛtvā sthāpayet tato vaktramātraṃ vihāya kṛtsnaṃ ghaṭāvayavaṃ mṛllepenācchādayet bhṛṣṭayantrākhye'smin yantre viṃśatipalamānaṃ śuddhaṃ sīsakaṃ dattvā tīvrottāpena dravīkuryāt tataḥ tasmin karṣapramāṇaṃ śodhitapāradaṃ prakṣipya darvyā ghaṭṭayet miśrībhūte ca tasmin pratyekaṃ palamānaṃ arjunādīnāṃ kṣāraṃ pṛthak pṛthak dattvā lauhadarvyā dṛḍhaṃ ghaṭṭayan tīvrāgninā viṃśatirātraṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: Here the operation is this: after making a curved furnace, one should place above it a single pot, making its mouth curved. Then, leaving only the mouth, one should cover the whole body of the pot with a coating of clay. In this apparatus called a roasting apparatus, after putting in twenty palas of purified lead, one should melt it with very strong heat. Then one should throw into it one karṣa of purified mercury and stir it with a ladle. When it has become mixed, one should add separately one pala each of the alkalis beginning with <s>arjuna</s>, and, while stirring firmly with an iron ladle, cook it with a strong fire for twenty nights.
"With an iron implement" means with an iron ladle.
"Barbarous" means inferior.
"Mixed with dark powder" means joined with turmeric powder.
<s>Ajamodā</s> is <s>yamānī</s>, because it cleanses the interior.
<s>Ārakūṭa</s> is brass.

children.text: khoṭaṃ rasajāraṇabandhanadravyaviśeṣaṃ bhūnāgasattvasya rasajārakatvāt atra khoṭaśabdena ravakareṇurūpaṃ bhūnāgasattvaṃ bodhyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khoṭa</s> is a particular substance used for digesting and binding mercury. Because the essence of <s>bhūnāga</s> digests mercury, here the word <s>khoṭa</s> should be understood as the essence of <s>bhūnāga</s> in the form of particles like sand.
<s>Peṭakārī</s> is <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>.
<s>Kākatuṇḍī</s> is white <s>guñjā</s>.
<s>Vākucī</s> is <s>somarājī</s>.
<s>Devadālī</s> is <s>hastighoṣaka</s>.
<s>Karkoṭī</s> is <s>karkoṭaka</s>, called <s>kāṃkola</s> in common speech.
<s>Kuṇḍalī</s> is a sieve, a winding strainer.

children.text: aratnivistārā prasāritakaniṣṭhāṅgulibaddhamuṣṭihastapramāṇāyatā caturaṅgulavistṛtakarṇikārādivalkalanirmitā aratnivistāraveṣṭanī yuktā chāgacarmamaṇḍitā aśvapucchakeśasūkṣmavastraracitataladeśā sūkṣmataradravyacālanārtham aparavidhā cālanītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'A cubit in breadth' means a different kind of sieve: it has a winding strainer a cubit wide, made from bark such as <s>karṇikāra</s>, as long as a fist with the little finger extended and four fingers broad; it is covered with goat hide, and its lower part is made from horse-tail hair and fine cloth, for straining very fine substances.
<s>Śarkarā</s> is sand.
<s>Sitopalā</s> is hard; it is called <s>phulakaḍī</s> in common speech.

children.text: śikhitralakṣaṇe kokilā uktāḥ ataḥ kokilāśabdasyārtham āha kokilā iti ||
children.translated_text: In the description of <s>śikhitra</s>, <s>kokilā</s>s have been mentioned; therefore he explains the meaning of the word <s>kokilā</s> with '<s>kokilā</s>'.

children.text: cetitāṅgārāḥ taptāṅgārāḥ payaso vinā svayaṃ nirvāṇāḥ śāntāḥ cet te aṅgārāḥ kokilāḥ matāḥ kokilāḥ kaylā iti bhāṣā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Cetitāṅgāra</s>s are heated coals. If, without water, they are extinguished by themselves and become quiet, those coals are considered <s>kokilā</s>s. <s>Kokilā</s>s are called <s>kaylā</s> in common speech.

children.text: caṣakaṃ pānapātraṃ vāṭī glās iti prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: A <s>caṣaka</s> is a drinking vessel, commonly known as a bowl or glass.
<s>Kṣudraśiprā</s>s are small shells.
<s>Jātarūpa</s> is gold.

children.text: samutthitam iti antarbhūtaṇyarthaprayogas tena samutthāpitaṃ śoṣitamityartha ūrdhvapātanāyantre sādhitamityartho vā ||
children.translated_text: 'Raised up' is a usage with a causative sense included; therefore it means 'made to rise,' or 'dried,' or else 'prepared in an upward-sublimation apparatus.'
That is the operation of raising up.
'<s>Kṛṣṭi</s>,' thus.
That operation with gold and silver should be understood as <s>kṛṣṭi</s>.

children.text: rasādibhiḥ saha svarṇaṃ vā raupyaṃ vā kenacinmārakadravyeṇa saṃmardya bahuśaḥ ātape śoṣayed athavā rasagandhādibhirmāritaṃ svarṇaṃ raupyaṃ vā bahuvāram ūrdhvapātanayantreṇa samutthāpayet sā kriyā kṛṣṭī bodhyā ||
children.translated_text: Gold or silver, together with mercury and the like, should be triturated with some killing substance and dried repeatedly in the sun; or gold or silver killed with mercury, sulfur, and the like should be raised up many times by an upward-sublimation apparatus. That operation should be understood as <s>kṛṣṭi</s>.

children.text: pūrvarītyā kṛtayā suvarṇaraupyayor anyatarakṛṣṭyā saha suvarṇaṃ saṃmardya puṭanena svarṇasya varṇānyatā na jāyate ||
children.translated_text: When gold is triturated together with a <s>kṛṣṭi</s> of either gold or silver prepared in the preceding manner, no alteration of color occurs in the gold through heating in a sealed crucible.

children.text: bījaṃ nirvāpaṇaviśeṣeṇa ityādinā vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇo dhātuviśeṣāṇāṃ vicitrasaṃskāraviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bīja</s> is a particular wondrous refinement of certain metals, whose definition will be stated below with the words beginning 'by a special quenching.'
A <s>bīja</s> made from gold-<s>kṛṣṭi</s> prepared in just the stated manner will color mercury.
He states the method presently concerning noble metal with '<s>tāmra</s>'.
'Joined with sharp' means joined with sharp iron.
'Many times' means seven times.

children.text: tīkṣṇalauhaṃ tāmraṃ ca agnisaṃtāpena dravīkṛtya gandhakacūrṇamiśritalakucarase nikṣiped ghanībhūtaṃ taddvayamuttolya punaḥ drāvayitvā pūrvarase nikṣiped evaṃ saptavārān ||
children.translated_text: Sharp iron and copper should be melted by the heat of fire and placed in the juice of <s>lakuca</s> mixed with sulfur powder. When the two have solidified, one should lift them out, melt them again, and place them in the same juice as before. This is to be done seven times.

children.text: drutamityatra mṛtam iti pāṭho mṛtaṃ bhasmībhūtam ||
children.translated_text: Where the reading is '<s>drutam</s>' there is also the reading '<s>mṛtam</s>': '<s>mṛta</s>' means reduced to ash.
By this procedure, excellent iron will come out from it; such is the meaning.
He explains copper-lead with '<s>mākṣika</s>'.

children.text: svarṇamākṣikeṇa saha māritaṃ tāmraṃ tathā sīsakaṃ ca pṛthak pṛthak daśavāraṃ samutthāpitaṃ kṛtvā tayoḥ pratyekaṃ catuṣpalaṃ ādāya ekīkuryāttataḥ tadubhayaṃ bhūyaḥ nīlāñjanena saha bhasmīkṛtya saptavāraṃ samutthāpayed evaṃ ca tayoḥ śulvanāga iti saṃjñā jāyate iti ||
children.translated_text: Copper killed together with gold <s>mākṣika</s>, and similarly lead, should each be raised up ten times separately. Taking four <s>pala</s>s of each, one should combine them. Then both together should again be incinerated with <s>nīlāñjana</s> and raised up seven times. In this way the designation <s>śulvanāga</s> arises for them.
He explains the designation <s>candrārka</s> with '<s>bhāgāḥ</s>'.
'<s>Bhāsvat</s>' means copper.

children.text: ekatrāvartitāḥ ekasminneva pātre yugapad dravīkṛtya āloḍitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Melted together in one place' means melted simultaneously in one and the same vessel and stirred.
'By that' means by that kind of stirring.
He states the definition of line-filled metal with '<s>aṅguṣṭha</s>'.

children.text: tadrekhāntare tayoḥ tarjanyaṅguṣṭhayoḥ rekhāntare rekhāvakāśe aṅguṣṭhatarjanībhyāṃ gharṣaṇe kṛte yatra lauhe tayoraṅgulyoḥ rekhāsamūhaḥ aṅkito bhavedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Between those lines' means in the space between the lines of the forefinger and thumb: when rubbing is done with thumb and forefinger, the collection of lines of those fingers becomes marked on the metal in question.
He states the definition of non-rising metal with '<s>guḍa</s>'.

children.text: sukhasparśaḥ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ nirutthīkārakamitrapañcakavarge ṭaṅkaṇaśabdagrahaṇāt yaduktaṃ rasendrasāre
children.translated_text: 'Pleasant to the touch' refers to borax, since the word <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is included in the group of five friends that make metals non-rising, as stated in the <s>Rasendrasāra</s>:
'Honey, ghee, <s>guñjā</s>, borax, and <s>guggulu</s> likewise,
this is reckoned as the group of five friends in the combining of metals.'
Thus.
Here the function of the <s>guggulu</s> mentioned in the group of five friends is to be accomplished by molasses.
'Nature' means its own form.
'<s>Apunarbhava</s>' means not rising again, that is, <s>niruttha</s>.
He states another definition of <s>niruttha</s> with '<s>raupya</s>'.

children.text: raupyaṃ lauhaṃ ca ekatra saṃsthāpya bhastrayā dhmāpanena yadi parasparaṃ miśrībhavet tadāpi nirutthaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: If silver and metal are placed together and, by blowing with bellows, become mutually mixed, then that too should be known as <s>niruttha</s>.
He explains <s>bīja</s> with '<s>nirvāpaṇa</s>'.

children.text: pūrvanirdiṣṭasādhyalohe tattallohamārakānyalohanikṣeparūpanirvāhaṇākhyasaṃskāraviśeṣeṇa yadā sādhyalohaṃ prakṣiptalauhavarṇaṃ bhavet tadā mṛdulaṃ sukhasparśaṃ citrasaṃskāram āhitāpūrvaguṇāntaraṃ tat bījamiti jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: When, by the special process called <s>nirvāhaṇa</s>, consisting of the insertion of another metal that kills each respective metal into the previously specified metal to be treated, the treated metal takes on the color of the inserted metal, then that soft, pleasant-to-touch substance, wondrously refined and endowed with a new additional quality, should be known as <s>bīja</s>.
He explains <s>uttaraṇa</s> with '<s>idam</s>'.
'This' means the form that will be stated below with the words beginning 'of the two combined metals.'
<s>Uttaraṇa</s> is a special technical designation.

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭeti miśritalauhayoḥ ekalohasya parināśanaṃ dhmāpanādikriyāviśeṣeṇa ekasmāt anyat pṛthakkṛtya bhasmīkaraṇam ekasmād anyasya bahirniṣkāśanaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: "Mixed" means, in the case of mixed metals, the destruction of one metal by a particular operation such as blowing, after separating one from another and reducing it to ash, or the extraction of one out from another.
He explains striking with the word "well-blown."
That is one metal of the two mixed metals, produced by the operation of extraction.
He explains <s>sattva</s> with the word "alkaline."

children.text: kṣāraḥ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ lauhaśodhakatvāt amlaḥ kāñjikādikaṃ drāvakaḥ guñjāṭaṅkaṇamadhvājyaguḍāḥ drāvakapañcakāḥ ityuktasvarūpaḥ taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Alkali is borax, because it purifies metals; acid is a solvent such as sour gruel. By these, whose nature is stated in the saying, "<s>guñjā</s>, borax, honey, ghee, and molasses are the five solvents."
"In the mine-furnace" means in the furnace-apparatus.
The essence is the stable part, that is to say, the clarified portion.
He explains <s>ekakolīsaka</s> with the word "furnace."

children.text: koṣṭhikāyantrāgrabhāgaparyantam aṅgārairāpūrya dhmāpanavaśāt māraṇīyadravyaiḥ mūṣākaṇṭhaparyantamāgataiḥ upalakṣito yat karma ekakolīsakākhyaḥ kriyāviśeṣo mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The operation marked by filling up to the front part of the furnace-apparatus with charcoal and, by means of blowing, bringing the substances to be incinerated up to the neck of the crucible is regarded as the special operation called <s>ekakolīsaka</s>.
He explains the characteristic of <s>varanāga</s> with the word "sharp."

children.text: atra viśeṣyapadollekhābhāve 'pi varanāga iti saṃjñābalādeva tīkṣṇanīlāñjanopetamityatra nāgamiti viśeṣyapadaṃ śeṣaḥ bodhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, although the qualified word is not explicitly stated, by the force of the technical name <s>varanāga</s> itself one should understand that the word to be supplied in "combined with sharp blue-black collyrium" is "lead."

children.text: tīkṣṇalauhanīlāñjanasaṃyuktaṃ yat sīsakaṃ bahuvāraṃ dṛḍham ādhmātaṃ sat sukomalaṃ kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ drutadrāvaṃ ca syāt tat sīsakaṃ varanāgaṃ bodhyam ||
children.translated_text: Lead which is combined with sharp iron and blue-black collyrium, strongly blown many times, and thereby becomes very soft, black in color, and quick to melt, should be understood as <s>varanāga</s>.

children.text: tīkṣṇamiti pṛthak pāṭhe nīlāñjanaṃ tīkṣṇalauhaṃ ca ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the reading is separately "sharp," the meaning is "blue-black collyrium and sharp iron."
He explains revivification with the word "of the dead."
Re-arising means the restoration of its own form through the application of apparatus and the like.
He explains washed metal with the words beginning "earth-snake."
"Removed" means diminished, drawn off, or expelled.
Dust is the powder of charcoal and the like adhering to it at the time of heating in a closed vessel and similar operations.
That refers to lead and tin which have become volatile.

children.text: bhūnāgamalarasaiḥ tanmalamiśrajalairvā pariśodhitamalādikaṃ kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ capalībhūtaṃ nāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca dhautanāgaṃ dhautavaṅgaṃ ca proktam iti niṣkarṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The conclusion is that black lead and tin that have become volatile and whose impurities and the like have been purified with the juices of earth-worm impurities, or with water mixed with their impurities, are called washed lead and washed tin.
He explains <s>dvandvāna</s> with the words "of two substances."
When a pair of mixed substances has been rubbed together, the designation <s>dvandvāna</s> arises through blowing.
For <s>dvandvāna</s> there is the variant reading <s>bandhana</s>, "binding."
He explains <s>bhañjanī</s> with the word "from the portion."

children.text: varṇena suvarṇa iva tasmin varṇasuvarṇake rājapittale bhāgāt māraṇārthanirdiṣṭaprakṣepyabhāgam apekṣya dravyādhikakṣepaṃ dravyāṇāṃ prakṣepyadravyāṇām adhikakṣepam adhikaprakṣepam anu paścād adhikaprakṣepānantaram ityarthaḥ yaḥ vahnikāgrāsaḥ māraṇīyadravyagatavahninirvāpaṇaṃ vāthavā dravair jalādibhiḥ yaḥ vahnikāgrāsaḥ sa bhañjanīti saṃjñayā vādibhiḥ rasavādibhiḥ matā kathitā ||
children.translated_text: In that color-gold, that is, royal brass, gold-like in color, after an excessive addition of substances beyond the portion of ingredients prescribed for incineration, that excess addition of the substances to be added, or after that excess addition, whatever consumption of fire occurs, meaning the extinguishing of the fire present in the substance to be incinerated, or whatever consumption of fire occurs by liquids such as water, is considered by the speakers, the alchemical authorities, to have the designation <s>bhañjanī</s>.
He explains <s>cullakā</s> with the word "pataṅgī."

children.text: pataṅgīkalkataḥ pataṅgīkalkāntar ityarthaḥ katiciddināni sthitvā lauhaṃ tāraṃ ceti śeṣaḥ tatra lauhe viśeṣataḥ tāre ca yā hematā svarṇasādṛśyaṃ jātā asau hematā cullakā yāti cullakā iti saṃjñāṃ labhate ityarthaḥ iti matā ||
children.translated_text: "From <s>pataṅgī</s> paste" means inside <s>pataṅgī</s> paste. After remaining for some days, iron and silver are to be supplied. The gold-like condition, the resemblance to gold, that especially arises there in iron and also in silver, goes to <s>cullakā</s>, that is, receives the designation <s>cullakā</s>; so it is considered.
<s>Cullakā</s> is called gilt in common speech.

children.text: yadvā lakṣaṇadvayamidaṃ tena pataṅgītyārabhya hematā ityantena ślokārdhena hematālakṣaṇam dinānītyādiślokārdhena ca cullakālavaṇaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Or else these are two definitions: by this, with the half-verse beginning <s>pataṅgī</s> and ending with "gold-like condition," the definition of <s>hematā</s> is to be known, and with the half-verse beginning "days" the <s>cullakā</s> salt is to be known.

children.text: asmin pakṣe vakṣyamāṇapataṅgīrāgākhyarañjakadravyaviśeṣasya kalkalepanena sarvalauhe viśeṣataḥ raupye hematā iti saṃjñā jāyate ||
children.translated_text: On this interpretation, by the application of a paste of the particular coloring substance later called <s>pataṅgīrāga</s>, the designation <s>hematā</s> arises in every metal, especially in silver.
<s>Hematā</s>, the state of gold, means resemblance to gold.

children.text: tathā asau lauhatārayor hematā katiciddināni sthitvā pataṅgīkalke ityāśayaḥ cullakā yāti cullaketyākhyayā khyātiṃ yātītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, the intention is that this gold-like state of iron and silver remains for some days in <s>pataṅgī</s> paste; it goes to <s>cullakā</s>, meaning it becomes known by the name <s>cullakā</s>.

children.text: pūrvaśloke pataṅgī ityuktam ataḥ tāmeva vivṛṇoti rañjitāditi ||
children.translated_text: Since <s>pataṅgī</s> was mentioned in the previous verse, he explains that very thing with the word "colored."

children.text: cirāddīrghakālaṃ vyāpya rañjitād vakṣyamāṇaraktādivargānyatamavargeṇa rāgapariprāptād yasmāt kasmādapi lauhād athavā cirakālataḥ sudīrghakālaṃ dhmānāddhmāpitād yasmāt kasmādapi rañjitalauhād yaḥ viniryāsaḥ niḥsravaḥ sattvamiti yāvat nirgacchatīti śeṣaḥ sa pataṅgīrāgasaṃjñakaḥ nirdiṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From any metal colored over a long time, that is, brought to coloration by one of the classes such as the red class to be described below, or from any colored metal blown over a very long time, whatever outflow emerges, the essence, so to speak, is designated <s>pataṅgīrāga</s>.
He explains sprinkling with the word "when melted."
"Standing in the fire" means situated right on top of the blazing hearth.

children.text: aṣṭanimeṣakam aṣṭavāram akṣṇor nimīlanonmīlanātmakaṃ kālaṃ viramya dravībhavanānantaram apekṣya ||
children.translated_text: "For eight blinks" means waiting, after melting, for the time consisting of eight openings and closings of the eyes.
He explains steaming with the words "with alkalis and acids."
"With medicines" means with the juices and the like of the various metal-purifying substances in question.

children.text: malaśaithilyakārakaṃ svedanena mārdave jāte antarmalānāṃ pṛthakkaraṇaṃ vīkaraṇaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: When softness has arisen through steaming, which loosens impurities, it is the separation or alteration of the internal impurities.
He explains rubbing with the word "with the stated."

children.text: uditairauṣadhaiḥ tatra tatroktabheṣajadravyāṇāṃ svarasaiḥ kvāthairvā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "With the stated medicines" means with the juices or decoctions of the medicinal substances mentioned in each respective place.
He explains stupefaction with the word "from rubbing."
By the desired medicines, namely by drugs considered suitable as purifiers and the like.
"Causing the condition of lost paste" means the state of being fixed in form, because through grinding its own form is destroyed.
"Tin," and so on.
This means the destruction of defects in lead, tin, and the like.

children.text: etattu rasam uddiśya uktaṃ dhātvantarāṇām api svasvadoṣanāśanam iti ādipadena bodhyam ||
children.translated_text: This, however, is stated with reference to <s>rasa</s> (mercury); by the word "and so on" it should be understood that other metals too have their own defects destroyed.
He states <s>utthāpana</s> (raising) with the word beginning "by sweating."

children.text: svedaḥ ūrdhvapātanādinā svedanam ātapaḥ raudrasaṃtāpaḥ ādinā mardanādīnām grahaṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sveda</s> is heating by upward sublimation and the like; <s>ātapa</s> is heating by the sun's heat; by "and so on" rubbing and similar operations are included.
"Making it attain its own form" means establishing it in its natural state.
"Removing the calamity of swooning" means preventing the misfortune consisting in destruction of its own form, produced by the operation of swooning.
He states binding with the words beginning "of its own form."

children.text: piṣṭam iṣṭabhaiṣajyaiḥ peṣaṇaṃ piṣṭamiti bhāvoktaḥ tasya bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Piṣṭa</s> is grinding with desired medicines; the word <s>piṣṭa</s> is used abstractly, meaning the condition of that.

children.text: tattvāt svarūpasya vināśena svakīyaśubhratvacapalatvādirūpāpāyena yad rūpāpādanam iti śeṣastad bandhanaṃ vahninānucchidyamānatvaṃ mūrtibaddhatvam iti vā jñeyam iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of that, the completion should be understood as follows: the bringing about of a form through destruction of its own form, that is, through the disappearance of its own whiteness, mobility, and so on, is called <s>bandhana</s> (binding), the condition of not being broken apart by fire, or else the state of being fixed in form.
He states another name for this very thing, <s>naṣṭapiṣṭi</s> (lost paste), with the word beginning "by the learned."

children.text: nirjito bandhanena naṣṭasvarūpaḥ yadvā nirjito mṛtaḥ sa sūtaḥ vidvadbhir naṣṭapiṣṭir ucyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> (mercury), conquered by binding and with its own form destroyed, or else conquered, that is, killed, is called <s>naṣṭapiṣṭi</s> by the learned.
He states the three kinds of sublimation with the words beginning "by the stated medicines."
<s>Niryātana</s> means tormenting done for the sake of purification and the like.
He states <s>rodhana</s> (confinement) with the word beginning "water."

children.text: jalasaindhavābhyāṃ saha kumbhamadhye divasatrayaṃ rasasya yā āsthāpanī ā samyak sthāpanī ṣaṇḍhadoṣanāśanapūrvakaṃ svavīrye sthāpanakāriṇī kriyeti śeṣaḥ asau sthitiḥ sthāpanaṃ rodhanamityucyate ||
children.translated_text: Together with water and rock salt, the placing of mercury in a jar for three days, that is, a complete placing, is an operation that establishes it in its own potency after first destroying the defect of impotence; that state is called <s>sthāpana</s> (establishing) or <s>rodhana</s>.

children.text: idaṃ hi svedanādikriyājanitakadarthanena ṣaṇḍhabhāvaprāptasya rasasya taddoṣanāśapūrvakavīryaprakarṣādhānārthaṃ jñātavyam ||
children.translated_text: This should be understood as intended to impart excellence of potency, after destroying that defect, to mercury that has reached a state of impotence because of the torment produced by operations such as heating.
In another treatise this is designated by the name <s>bodhana</s> (awakening).
He states <s>niyamana</s> (restraining) with the word beginning "after confinement."
<s>Sveda</s> means heating.

children.text: yadyapyatra svedanārthaṃ dravyanirdeśo na kṛtaḥ tathāpi adhyetṝṇāṃ vijñānārthaṃ granthāntaroktaṃ tannirdiśyate tathā ca rasendracintāmaṇau
children.translated_text: Although here the substances for heating are not specified, nevertheless, for the students' understanding, what is stated in another treatise is now specified. Thus in the <s>Rasendracintāmaṇi</s>:
"With the waters of <s>sarpākṣī</s>, <s>ciñcikā</s>, <s>kanyā</s>, <s>bhṛṅgāraka</s>, and <s>kanaka</s>,

children.text: dinaṃ saṃsveditaḥ sūto niyamāt sthiratāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: mercury heated for one day certainly becomes steady."
Thus.
<s>Niyamana</s> is the production of steadiness after the removal of mobility.
He states <s>dīpana</s> (kindling) with the word beginning "metal."
The completion is: for the sake of consuming solid gold and the like as a morsel.

children.text: svedaḥ dolāyantre kāñjikādinā rasasya iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sveda</s> means heating mercury in a swing-apparatus with sour gruel and the like.
<s>Dīpana</s> is a particular operation that generates the power to consume a morsel.
The author of the <s>Rasendracintāmaṇi</s> states different substances for kindling, as follows:
"Green vitriol, the five salts, mustard seed, and pepper,
together with <s>bhūśigru</s> seed and borax,
are stirred in sour gruel and cooked in a swing-apparatus for three days;
then proper kindling of the king of mercury takes place for digestion.
Or else one should cook it for three days in sour gruel with juices of <s>citraka</s>."
Thus.
He states the measure of the morsel with the words beginning "of such measure."

children.text: iyanmānasya etāvatparimāṇasya sūtasya saṃbandhavivakṣayā ṣaṣṭhī iyanmite sūte ityarthaḥ yā iyatī mitiḥ etāvatparimāṇaṃ bhojyadravyāṇām iti śeṣaḥ iti ucyate bhojyadravyātmikā grasanīyasvarṇādidravyāṇāṃ mānanirdeśarūpā asau uktiḥ grāsamānaṃ samīritam iyanmānaḥ sūtaḥ iyanmānaṃ svarṇādidravyaṃ grasituṃ samarthaḥ evaṃrūpamānanirdeśaḥ grāsamānaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: "Of such measure" means of this much quantity; the genitive is used with reference to the relation of mercury, that is, "when the mercury has such measure." The statement saying, "the measure of the edible substances is so much," that is, specifying the measure of gold and other substances to be consumed, is called <s>grāsamāna</s> (morsel-measure). One should understand <s>grāsamāna</s> as a specification of measure of this sort: mercury of such a measure is capable of consuming gold and other substances of such a measure.
He states the threefold <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion) with the word beginning "of the morsel."

children.text: grāsasya grāsayogyasya svarṇāderityarthaṃ cāraṇaṃ rasāntaḥ kṣepaṇaṃ garbhe drāvaṇaṃ rasāntaḥ taralībhavanaṃ jāraṇaṃ viḍayantrādiyogena dravībhūtagrāsasya pākaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The insertion of the morsel, that is, of gold and the like fit to be consumed, into mercury is <s>cāraṇa</s>; melting in the womb means becoming liquid inside the mercury; <s>jāraṇa</s> is the cooking, through the use of the <s>viḍa</s>-apparatus and so forth, of the liquefied morsel.
He states another threefold division of <s>jāraṇā</s> with the word beginning "morsel."
<s>Grāsa</s> is digestion in the form of making a mouthful; <s>piṇḍa</s> is digestion in the form of becoming a lump like mud.
<s>Parīṇāma</s> is digestion in the form of bringing about another state.
Among these, first he states mouthless digestion with the word beginning "mouthless."

children.text: niḥ nāsti mukhaṃ vakṣyamāṇacatuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśaḥ bījaprakṣeparūpamukhalakṣaṇaṃ yatra jāraṇāyāṃ tādṛśī ||
children.translated_text: It is that digestion in which there is no <s>mukha</s>, no "mouth" characterized by the insertion of seed in a sixty-fourth part, which will be described below.
"Seed," and so on.

children.text: bhāgataḥ yathābhāgaṃ tattaddravyajāraṇāyāṃ nirdiṣṭabhāgam anatikramya vakṣyamāṇacatuḥṣaṣṭibhāgāt nyūnatayā adhikatayā vā ityarthaḥ bījādānena śuddhasvarṇaraupyātmakabījagrahaṇam ||
children.translated_text: "By parts" means according to the proper part: in the digestion of each respective substance, not exceeding the specified part, that is, being less or greater than the sixty-fourth part to be described below. By taking seed is meant taking seed consisting of purified gold and silver.
He states digestion with a mouth with the word beginning "thus."
When this has been done, that is, when seed has been inserted in a sixty-fourth part,
it is "with a mouth," <s>samukha</s>.
<s>Mṛgacārin</s> was a certain author of a rasa-tantra bearing that name.
He states the demon-mouthed mercury with the word beginning "divine herb."
The divine herb is realgar.
"In open furnaces" means in apparatuses whose furnace-mouths are uncovered.
"It should eat" means it should consume.
He states the definition of <s>cāraṇa</s>, a subdivision of <s>jāraṇā</s>, with the word beginning "of mercury."

children.text: jaṭhare madhye ityarthaḥ grāsakṣapaṇaṃ grāsasya grāsārhalauhādeḥ kṣapaṇaṃ kṣayamāpādanaṃ rasena saha ekīkaraṇamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "In the belly" means in the middle. <s>Grāsakṣapaṇa</s> is the destruction of the morsel, that is, bringing to dissolution the morsel fit for consumption, such as metal; in other words, making it one with the <s>rasa</s> (mercurial substance).
In connection with internal liquefaction he explains external liquefaction with the word "outside."

children.text: bahir eva cullyuparisthakaṭāhādau na tu rasagarbhe ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is only outside, on a pan placed above the stove and the like, not inside the belly of the <s>rasa</s>; that is the meaning.

children.text: ghanasattvādikam abhrasattvādikam atrādipadena svarṇasattvādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ bodhyam ||
children.translated_text: "Dense essence and the like" means mica essence and the like. Here, by the word "and the like," essences such as gold-essence are to be understood as included.
He states the fivefold divisions of liquefaction with the word beginning "non-adherence."

children.text: nirlepatvaṃ niḥ niścayena niḥśeṣeṇa vā lepatvaṃ liptatvaṃ drāvāntareṇa saha niḥśeṣeṇa ekībhavanamityarthaḥ yadvā niḥ nirgataḥ lepaḥ liptapadārthaḥ malādiryasmāt tattvaṃ pṛthagbhūtamalādikam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nirlepatva</s> means the state of being without coating: either surely or completely being coated, that is, becoming entirely one with another liquid. Or else it means the condition in which the coating, the adhered substance such as impurity, has gone away; in other words, the impurity and so forth has become separate.
<s>Drutatva</s> is liquefaction in a special sense.
<s>Tejastva</s> is predominance of fiery brilliance with respect to its own nature.
<s>Laghutā</s> is lightness in comparison with its natural heaviness.

children.text: asaṃyogaśca sūtena pāradena saha pṛthaktayā avasthānam ||
children.translated_text: And non-conjunction is remaining separate from <s>sūta</s>, that is, mercury.
He explains the kind of assimilation called assimilation by liquefaction with the word beginning "liquefied."

children.text: viḍaḥ vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇalakṣitaḥ yantraṃ koṣṭhikādikaṃ tadādiyogataḥ atrādipadena mūṣāpuṭādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ drutasya garbhe taralitasya grāsasya svarṇādeḥ parīṇāmaḥ paripākaḥ svātmani abhedarūpeṇa pariṇamanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viḍa</s> is characterized by the definition to be stated later. The apparatus is a furnace and the like; by the word "and the like" here, crucibles, sealed heating, and so forth are included. The transformation of a liquefied morsel, such as gold, within the belly means its digestion, its becoming transformed within itself in the form of non-difference.

children.text: rasendracintāmaṇau tu jāraṇā hi pātanagālanavyatirekeṇa ghanahemādigrāsapūrvakaṃ pūrvāvasthāpannatvam ityanena yat prakārāntaraṃ jāraṇālakṣaṇamuktaṃ tat cāraṇākhyajāraṇābhiprāyeṇa bodhyam ||
children.translated_text: But in the <s>Rasendracintāmaṇi</s>, another definition of <s>jāraṇā</s> is given: "assimilation is the entering into a former state, preceded by a morsel of solid gold and the like, apart from sublimation and filtering." That should be understood as intended for the assimilation called <s>cāraṇā</s>.
He explains coloring with the word beginning "well accomplished."

children.text: śodhitasvarṇaraupyābhyāṃ tathā jīrṇatāmrādiyogena kriyāviśeṣam āśritya rasasya yat pītādirāgajananam ityanvayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The construction is: by purified gold and silver, and likewise through combination with digested copper and the like, depending on a particular operation, there is the production in the <s>rasa</s> of a yellow color and the like.
He explains <s>sāraṇā</s> with the word beginning "in the <s>sūta</s>."

children.text: satailayantrasthe tailapūrṇāndhamūṣāmadhyasthite sūte rase yat svarṇādikṣepaṇaṃ svarṇādiprakṣepaḥ lohe tāmrādau ityarthaḥ vedhādhikyakaraṃ vedhasya svarṇādijananarūpavedhaśakteḥ ādhikyakaram ātiśayyajanakam ||
children.translated_text: When <s>sūta</s>, that is <s>rasa</s>, is located in an oil-filled blind crucible placed in an oil apparatus, the throwing in of gold and the like, that is the insertion of gold and so forth, into a metal such as copper, increases <s>vedha</s>; that is, it produces an excellence of the penetrating power called <s>vedha</s>, whose form is the production of gold and the like.
And it is said in the <s>Rasendracintāmaṇi</s>:
Now <s>sāraṇā</s> is explained.
A blind crucible should be made resembling the shape of a cow's udder.
That very crucible, furnished with a hole in the middle and deep, is suitable for <s>sāraṇā</s>.

children.text: asyām eva mūṣāyāṃ tattailam apagatakalkavimalam āpūryam asminnadhikam adhastād drutabījaprakṣepasamakālam eva samāvarjanīyaḥ sūtavarastadanu sadyo mūṣānanam ācchādanīyam ||
children.translated_text: This oil, free from sediment and clear, is to be poured into this very crucible; at the same time as the liquefied seed is thrown in from below, the excellent <s>sūta</s> should be poured into it in larger quantity, and immediately afterward the mouth of the crucible should be covered.

children.text: etat tailāktakhaṇḍagranthibandhena aruṇāsitabījābhyām aśvanāsārakarmaṇā militaścet sāritaḥ samyak saṃyamitaḥ vijñātavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, through tying with knots of pieces smeared with this oil and through the operation called horse-nose, it is joined with red and black seeds, then it should be known to have been properly subjected to <s>sāraṇā</s> and restrained.
The oil for <s>sāraṇā</s> too should be sought there itself; it has not been quoted because of fear of prolixity. Thus.

children.text: sāraṇālakṣaṇe vedhādhikyakaram ityuktaṃ kastāvat vedha ityapekṣāyāmāha vyavāyīti nāgavallīkumārikādhustūrādivyavāyiguṇavadbheṣajasaṃyuktaḥ ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the definition of <s>sāraṇā</s> it was said, "increases <s>vedha</s>." When the question arises, "What, then, is <s>vedha</s>?" he explains with the word "diffusive": it means joined with medicines possessing the diffusive quality, such as betel, aloe, and thorn-apple.
The definition of <s>vyavāyin</s> in <s>Śārṅgadhara</s> is as follows:

children.text: pūrvaṃ vyāpyākhilaṃ kāyaṃ tataḥ pākaṃ ca gacchati
children.translated_text: First it pervades the whole body, and then it undergoes digestion;
that is <s>vyavāyin</s>, as are hemp, opium, and what arises from a snake.
Thus.
"In the substance" means in the metal that one wishes to transform into the form of gold and the like.
Among these he explains the definition of <s>lepavedha</s> with the word "application."
"Application" is intended as application with <s>rasa</s> perfected by a special operation that produces the capacity for <s>vedha</s>.
Here, in <s>lepavedha</s>,

children.text: saurakaṃ puṭaṃ dadyāditi śeṣaḥ sūryapakvaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the remainder is "one should give a solar heating"; the meaning is that one should cook it by the sun.
He explains the definition of <s>kṣepavedha</s> with the word "throwing in."

children.text: galitasvarṇetaralauhe rasaprakṣepeṇa yat suvarṇīkaraṇaṃ sa kṣepākhyavedho jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The making into gold that occurs by throwing <s>rasa</s> into molten metal other than gold is to be known as the <s>vedha</s> called <s>kṣepa</s>.
He explains <s>kuntavedha</s> with the word beginning "with tongs."

children.text: saṃdaṃśaḥ sāṃḍāśī iti khyātaḥ saṃdaṃśayantreṇa mūrtibaddhasūtaṃ dhṛtvā drutalauhe nimajjanena tatsamparkāt svarṇādirūpeṇa pariṇatasya lauhasya yadāharaṇaṃ sa kuntavedhasaṃjñako jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A <s>saṃdaṃśa</s> is what is known as tongs. When embodied, fixed <s>sūta</s> is held with a tong apparatus and dipped into molten metal, and by contact with it the metal is transformed into the form of gold and the like and then drawn out, that is to be known by the name <s>kuntavedha</s>.
He explains <s>dhūmavedha</s> with the word beginning "in the fire."

children.text: sadhūmavahnimadhye vedhasamartharasanikṣepeṇa yo dhūmaḥ nirgacchati tatsamparkād yat kiṃcillohasya svarṇādirūpeṇa yā pariṇatiḥ sa dhūmavedhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When <s>rasa</s> capable of <s>vedha</s> is placed in a smoky fire, smoke comes forth; whatever transformation of metal into the form of gold and the like occurs by contact with that smoke is <s>dhūmavedha</s>.
He explains <s>śabdavedha</s> with the word beginning "mouth."
<s>Dhamana</s> means the utterance of sound; or the meaning is blowing.
The suffix <s>lyu</s> is added after the root <s>dham</s>, "to sound."

children.text: mukhamadhye vedhasamartharasaguṭikāṃ saṃsthāpya puro lauhakhaṇḍam ekaṃ dhṛtvā śabdoccāraṇe kṛte phutkāre datte vā tat lauhakhaṇḍaṃ svarṇādirūpeṇa pariṇamet ||
children.translated_text: After placing in the mouth a pill of <s>rasa</s> capable of <s>vedha</s>, and holding a piece of metal in front, when the utterance of sound is made, or when a puff is given, that piece of metal is transformed into the form of gold and the like.

children.text: dhamanāt ityatra damanāt iti pāṭhe mukhamadhye vedhasamartharasaguṭikāṃ saṃsthāpya kṣudralauhakhaṇḍaṃ tannimne nidhāya ca pīḍane kṛte adhaḥsthalauhakhaṇḍaṃ yatra vedhe svarṇādirūpeṇa pariṇamet sa śabdavedhaḥ ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the expression "from blowing," if the reading is "from suppressing," the meaning is this: after placing in the middle of the mouth a perfected mercury-pill capable of piercing, and after putting a small piece of iron below it, when pressure is applied, if that lower piece of iron is transformed, at the point of piercing, into the form of gold and the like, that is called <s>śabdavedha</s> (sound-piercing).
He states <s>udghāṭana</s> (opening) with the words "of a perfected substance."

children.text: siddhadravyasya mṛtalauhāder ityarthaḥ sūtena kriyāviśeṣaniṣpannasūtasaṃyogena yat kāluṣyādinivāraṇaṃ mālinyādiproñchanaṃ varṇasya ca prakāśanam aujjvalyasaṃpādanaṃ yadvā sūtena sūtasaṃyogena siddhadravyasya māritalohādeḥ kāluṣyādinivāraṇaṃ yayā kriyayā dravyāntarasaṃyogajanitamālinyādināśanaṃ syādityevaṃ yojanīyam ||
children.translated_text: "Of a perfected substance" means of dead iron and the like. By mercury, that is, by contact with mercury produced through a particular operation, the removal of blackness and so on, the wiping away of impurity and so on, and the manifestation of color, the production of brilliance, is intended. Or else it should be construed thus: by mercury, that is, by contact with mercury, there is for the perfected substance, such as killed metal, the removal of blackness and the like, by which operation the destruction of impurity and so on produced by contact with another substance occurs.

children.text: siddhadravyasya sūtena ityatra siddhadravyeṇa sūtasya iti pāṭhe mṛtalauhādisaṃyogadvārā sūtasya yat kāluṣyādinivāraṇam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the phrase "of the perfected substance by mercury," if the reading is "of mercury by the perfected substance," the meaning is the removal of blackness and so on from mercury by means of contact with dead iron and the like.
He states <s>svedana</s> (heating) with the word "with alkalis and acids."
"With medicines" means with medicines suitable for heating.
"The vessel" means the vessel filled with mercury.

children.text: atra uṣṇavīryaiḥ kṣārāmlaiḥ saha bhūmyadhaḥsthāpanena taduṣmaṇā anagnisvedo bodhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here one should understand heating without fire: through placing it underground together with alkalis and acids of hot potency, by means of their heat.
He states <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (depositing) with the words "of mercury."
"Joined with medicines" means joined with alkaline and acidic medicines.

children.text: mandāgniyutacullyantaḥ mṛdvagniviśiṣṭacullīmadhye na tu tīvrāgniyutacullyām ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Inside a stove with mild fire" means within a stove distinguished by gentle fire, and not in a stove with intense fire.
He states the swing-apparatus, <s>dolāyantra</s>, with the words "with a liquid substance."
"With a liquid substance" means with a heating liquid such as sour gruel.
"Of the mouth," and so on.
The meaning is that two holes are to be made at the two ends of the neck of the vessel.
"Of those two" means of those two holes.
"In the middle of it" means in the middle of the rod.

children.text: svedanārheṇa kāñjikādinā kenacit draveṇa bhāṇḍārdhamāpūrya bhāṇḍakandharāprāntadvaye chidradvayaṃ kṛtvā tanmadhye daṇḍamekaṃ nidhāya tasmin rasapoṭṭalīṃ baddhvā ca evaṃ lambayet yathā bhāṇḍasthadrave sā nimajjet paraṃ tu bhāṇḍam na spṛśediti niṣkarṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The conclusion is this: after filling half the vessel with some liquid suitable for heating, such as sour gruel, and after making two holes at the two ends of the neck of the vessel, one should place a single rod through them, tie the mercury bundle to it, and suspend it in such a way that it is immersed in the liquid in the vessel, but does not touch the vessel.
He states the form of the sublimation apparatus, <s>pātanayantra</s>, with the word "eight aṅgulas."
<s>Parīṇāha</s> means breadth, that is, circumference.
<s>Ānāha</s> means height, that is, length.
<s>Utsedha</s> means swelling, that is, thickness.
In the downward sublimation apparatus, he states the procedure of sublimation with the word "then."

children.text: atha uktarītyā yantranirmāṇānantaram ūrdhvabhājane uparisthādhomukhabhāṇḍodare ityarthaḥ ādau liptaṃ paścāt sthāpitaṃ tasya liptasthāpitasya rasasyeti śeṣaḥ jale adhobhāṇḍasthite iti śeṣaḥ dīptaiḥ vanotpalaiḥ vanyakarīṣāgnibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Then" means after the apparatus has been constructed in the manner stated. "In the upper vessel" means in the belly of the upper, downward-facing vessel. "First smeared, afterward placed" refers, by ellipsis, to the mercury that has been smeared and placed. "In water" means, by ellipsis, in the water situated in the lower vessel. "With blazing forest cow-dung cakes" means with fires made from wild cow-dung cakes.
He states the lamp-apparatus, <s>dīpikāyantra</s>, with the word "tortoise."

children.text: vakṣyamāṇakacchapayantramadhyavartimṛnmayaghaṭakharpararūpapīṭhopari pradīpamekam saṃsthāpya tatra sūtaṃ sthāpayet kacchapayantrādhaḥ vahniṃ ca dadyāt evaṃ pradīpasthasūtaḥ kacchapayantre patati tat dīpikākhyaṃ yantraṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: One should place a lamp on top of a base in the form of an earthen pot-sherd situated in the middle of the tortoise-apparatus to be described, and place mercury there; one should also apply fire beneath the tortoise-apparatus. In this way the mercury placed on the lamp falls into the tortoise-apparatus. That apparatus is to be known as called <s>dīpikā</s>.
He states the <s>ḍekīyantra</s> with the words "from the neck of the vessel."

children.text: bhāṇḍasya kaṇṭhanimne chidramekaṃ vidhāya tatra vaṃśanirmitaṃ nalamekaṃ saṃyojya sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made a single hole below the neck of the vessel, one should attach and set there a tube made of bamboo.

children.text: anyacca jalapūrṇakāṃsyapātradvayena saṃpuṭamekaṃ kṛtvā bhāṇḍakaṇṭhasthanalāgraṃ tatra praveśya dṛḍhaṃ sandhirodhaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Further, after making a single closed capsule with two bronze vessels filled with water, one should insert there the tip of the tube fixed in the vessel-neck and firmly seal the joint.

children.text: tato bhāṇḍamadhye nirdiṣṭadravyaiḥ saha rasaṃ kṣiptvā agnijvālā deyā tena nālacchidrānusārī rasaḥ kāṃsyapātramadhyasthajale patati ||
children.translated_text: Then, after putting mercury into the vessel together with the prescribed substances, a flame of fire is to be applied; by that, the mercury following the holes of the tube falls into the water in the bronze vessel.

children.text: evaṃ yāvat sarvaṃ pātraṃ uṣṇaṃ bhavet tāvat kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: One should do this until the whole vessel becomes hot.
<s>Rasasaṃdhāna</s> means the issuing forth of mercury.
He states the digestion-apparatus, <s>jāraṇāyantra</s>, with two verses beginning "iron."

children.text: vitastimānaṃ lauhamayamūṣādvayaṃ nirmāya tayorīṣacchidrānvitāyām ekasyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ gandhakaṃ saṃsthāpayet tataḥ rasagarbhāyāmanyasyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ pūrvoktāṃ sagandhakamūṣāṃ praveśya sūtagarbhamūṣādho jalaṃ sthāpayitvā ūrdhvādhaśca vahniṃ prajvālayediti ||
children.translated_text: After making two iron crucibles of the measure of a span, one should place sulfur in one of them, which has a slight hole. Then, after inserting that previously mentioned sulfur-containing crucible into another crucible containing mercury, and after placing water below the mercury-containing crucible, one should kindle fire both above and below.
He states the <s>vidyādharayantra</s> with the word "apparatus."
"From the enclosing capsule of two bowls" means from a special kind of closed capsule made with two cooking pots.
He explains that very thing with the word "stove."

children.text: adhobhāṇḍe auṣadhaṃ nikṣipya bhāṇḍāntareṇa mukhaṃ pidhāya cullyāṃ caturmukhyāṃ saṃsthāpya ca jvālā deyā ||
children.translated_text: After placing the medicine in the lower vessel, covering the mouth with another vessel, and setting it on a four-mouthed stove, a flame is to be applied.
<s>Koṣṭhīyantra</s> is another name for this.

children.text: granthāntare tu vidyādharayantralakṣaṇam anyavidhaṃ tattu agre svayameva vakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: In another treatise, however, the definition of the <s>vidyādharayantra</s> is different; that he himself will state later.
He states the <s>somānalayantra</s> with the word "above."
"Sky and so on" means mica and the like.

children.text: sthālīmadhye rasamūṣāṃ saṃsthāpya śarāveṇa mukhaṃ pidhāya mṛdvastreṇa sandhiṃ liptvā ca jalapūrṇasthālyantaropari sthālīṃ tāṃ sthāpayet śarāvopari karīṣāgniṃ ca dadyād iti ||
children.translated_text: Having placed the mercury-crucible in the pot, covered its mouth with a saucer, smeared the joint with clay-cloth, and set that pot upon another pot filled with water, one should put a cow-dung-cake fire on top of the saucer. Thus.
He explains the <s>garbhayantra</s> (womb-apparatus) with the word "<s>garbhayantra</s>."
"Paste" means mercury that has been made into a destroyed paste.

children.text: loṇasya lavaṇasya loṇasya ityatra lohasya iti pāṭhāntaraṃ na yuktaṃ lavaṇārdhamṛdambubhiḥ iti vakṣyamāṇavākyavirodhāt ||
children.translated_text: "Of <s>loṇa</s>" means of salt. In the expression "of <s>loṇa</s>," the variant reading "of iron" is not correct, because it conflicts with the statement to be made, "with water, clay, and half as much salt."

children.text: atra vāraṃ vāramiti padaṃ peṣayitvā tathā punaḥ punariti padaṃ mūṣālepamityanena yojanīyam ||
children.translated_text: Here the phrase "again and again" is to be construed with "after grinding," and likewise the phrase "repeatedly" with "the smearing of the crucible."

children.text: lavaṇārdhamṛdambubhiriti sahārthe tṛtīyā tena lavaṇārdhamṛdambubhiḥ saha loṇaguggulū peṣayitvā iti tathā viṃśatibhāgalavaṇāpekṣayā mṛdo'rdhatvamiti ca bodhyam ||
children.translated_text: In "with water, clay, and half as much salt," the instrumental is in the sense of accompaniment. Therefore it should be understood as "after grinding the salt and guggulu together with water and clay amounting to half the salt," and also that the clay is half in relation to twenty parts of salt.
"It should draw out" means it should dry in the sun.
He explains the <s>vālukāyantra</s> (sand apparatus) with the word beginning "wet."
"Wet" means containing mercury within.
"With concealed mouth" means having a narrow mouth.
"With clay," and so on.

children.text: mṛdvastreṇa mṛlliptavastreṇa aṅgulaghanaṃ aṅgulamānotsedhaṃ yathā tathā āvṛtām ||
children.translated_text: "With clay-cloth" means with cloth smeared with clay; "a finger thick" means covered so that it has a height of one finger-measure.

children.text: triṣu bhāgeṣu pūrayet pācyarasādinā kācakalasyāḥ bhāgatrayaṃ pūrayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "One should fill it in three parts" means that one should fill three parts of the glass jar with the mercury and other substance to be cooked.
In "in three parts," the locative indicates delimitation.
At "in the vessel," the ellipsis is: "one should place the glass jar."

children.text: vālukābhiḥ kiyān bhāgaḥ pūrayitavya ityapekṣāyāmāha tadbhāṇḍamiti ||
children.translated_text: When it is asked how much of the vessel should be filled with sand, he says this with the word beginning "that vessel."
At "with three,"
the ellipsis is "parts."

children.text: tṛtīyā cātra abhede bhāṇḍasya bhāgatrayamityarthaḥ pūrayet vālukayeti śeṣaḥ anyābhiḥ vālukābhirityarthaḥ avaśiṣṭāṃśaṃ pūrayediti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the instrumental is in the sense of non-difference, meaning "three parts of the vessel." The ellipsis is: "one should fill it with sand," that is, with other sand. The ellipsis is: "one should fill the remaining portion."

children.text: avaguṇṭhayedityasya maṇikayā ityanena sambandhaḥ maṇikayā śarāveṇa ||
children.translated_text: "One should cover" is connected with "with a jewel-shaped cover," meaning with a saucer.

children.text: ayamarthaḥ saṃkīrṇamukhīṃ kācakūpikāṃ mṛdvastreṇāṅgulotsedhamālipya śoṣayitvā ca tasyā bhāgatrayaṃ rasenāpūrayet tato vitastipramāṇagabhīre vālukayā tribhāgapūrṇe bhāṇḍamadhye tāṃ niveśya ūrdhvaṃ vālukayā ācchādayet tataśca śarāveṇa bhāṇḍavaktraṃ pidhāya mṛttikayā saṃdhiṃ liptvā ca tāvat pacet yāvat śarāvopari nyastaṃ tṛṇaṃ na dahediti ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: after smearing a narrow-mouthed glass bottle with clay-cloth to the height of a finger and drying it, one should fill three parts of it with mercury. Then, having set it in the middle of a vessel one span deep and filled to three parts with sand, one should cover it above with sand. Next, having covered the mouth of the vessel with a saucer and smeared the joint with clay, one should cook it until a blade of grass placed on top of the saucer does not burn.
Because its characteristics are the same, in the context of the <s>vālukāyantra</s> he also extends the instruction to the <s>lavaṇayantra</s> (salt apparatus) with the word "that."

children.text: tad uktaprakāraṃ yantraṃ lavaṇāśrayam api bhavatīti śeṣaḥ lavaṇayantram api vālukāyantram bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ellipsis is: that apparatus of the stated type may also have salt as its support. The meaning is that the <s>lavaṇayantra</s> too is a <s>vālukāyantra</s>.
He explains another kind of <s>vālukāyantra</s> with the word beginning "five."
The meaning is: in a vessel filled with sand measuring forty saucers.

children.text: atra vālukāmadhye eva rasagolādikaṃ sthāpayet na tu kācakūpyāmiti viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the particular point is that the mercury pellet and the like should be placed directly in the middle of the sand, not in a glass bottle.
He explains another type of <s>lavaṇayantra</s> with the word beginning "inside."

children.text: antas tāmrapātramadhye ityarthaḥ kṛtaḥ rasena ālepaḥ yatra tathābhūtaṃ yat tāmrapātraṃ tasya mukhaṃ tasya rasaliptodaratāmrapātramukhasya tathā bhāṇḍatalasya tāmrapātramukhopari sthāpitabhāṇḍādhobhāgasya ||
children.translated_text: "Inside" means in the middle of a copper vessel. "Made" means that a coating with mercury has been made; the mouth of such a copper vessel, that is, of a copper vessel whose inside is coated with mercury, and likewise the bottom of the vessel, that is, the lower part of the vessel placed upon the mouth of the copper vessel.
"That vessel" means the upper vessel.
"As before" means until the grass does not burn.

children.text: tāmrapātrodare rasaṃ nikṣipya tadupari lavaṇapūrṇaṃ kṣārapūrṇaṃ vā bhāṇḍamekaṃ vinyaset tato mṛllavaṇena sandhiṃ ruddhvā pacet iti ||
children.translated_text: Having placed mercury in the belly of a copper vessel, one should set upon it a vessel filled with salt or filled with alkali. Then, after closing the joint with clay and salt, one should cook it. Thus.
He explains the <s>nālikāyantra</s> (tube apparatus) with the word beginning "iron."

children.text: lauhamayanālamadhye pāradam āpūrya chidrarodhaṃ kṛtvā ca lavaṇapūritabhāṇḍāntaḥ nālaṃ taṃ nirundhyāttato maṇikayā bhāṇḍavaktram ācchādya ālipya ca sandhiṃ tāvat pacet yāvat śarāvoparisthaṃ tṛṇaṃ na dahet iti ||
children.translated_text: Having filled mercury into the middle of an iron tube and stopped the hole, one should confine that tube inside a vessel filled with salt. Then, after covering the vessel's mouth with a jewel-shaped cover and smearing the joint, one should cook it until a blade of grass lying on the saucer does not burn.
He explains the <s>puṭayantra</s> (covered-heating apparatus) with the word beginning "in a saucer."

children.text: karīṣeṣu pacet athavā agnimānavid dviyāmaṃ cullyām aṅgāreṣu paced yojyam ||
children.translated_text: It should be construed: one should cook it among cow-dung cakes, or else one who knows the measure of fire should cook it for two watches on a hearth among embers.
He explains the <s>koṣṭhīyantra</s> (furnace apparatus) with the word beginning "sixteen."

children.text: atra samamiti padena militabhāṇḍadvayasya ṣoḍaśāṅgulatvādi bodhyam evaṃ ca vitastipramāṇadīrghasya aṣṭāṅgulavistīrṇasya ca adhobhāṇḍasya mukhopari tāvanmānaṃ bhāṇḍāntaram adhomukhaṃ saṃsthāpya adho dṛḍhāṅgārair bhastrayā dhamet tena dhātusattvaṃ nirgacchatīti ||
children.translated_text: Here, by the word "equal," it should be understood that the two vessels joined together have a height of sixteen fingers and so on. Thus, after placing another vessel of the same measure face downward upon the mouth of the lower vessel, which is one span long and eight fingers wide, one should blow from below with a bellows through firm charcoal. By that, the essence of the metal comes out.
In the <s>Atrisaṃhitā</s>, after this verse another part of the same passage is read as follows:
"In the furnace below, completely filled with firm charcoal and with wind,
one should kindle the fire in due measure through the path of the flame."
Thus.
He explains the <s>valabhīyantra</s> with the word beginning "where."

children.text: valayadvayaṃ valayaṃ kaḍā āṃṭā iti khyātaṃ ||
children.translated_text: "Two rings" means rings, known as <s>kaḍā</s> and <s>āṃṭā</s>.
"Such" means made of iron.
"With a ring," and so on.

children.text: valaye bṛhatpātrasthavalaye protam ābaddhaṃ koṣṭhaṃ madhyadeśo yasya tādṛśam ||
children.translated_text: "In the ring" means that it has its chamber, that is, its middle region, threaded or bound in a ring, namely in the ring of a large vessel.

children.text: ayamartho bṛhadākāraṃ kāntalauhamayaṃ pātramekaṃ nirmāya tasyāntargalād adhaḥpārśvadvaye valayadvayaṃ saṃyojanīyaṃ kṣudrākāram aparamapi tathāvidhaṃ pātramekaṃ kṛtvā bṛhatpātrasthe valaye aspṛṣṭatalabhāgaṃ yathā tathā ābadhya tatra mūrchitarasaṃ parikṣipet kāñjikena sthūlapātraṃ ca pūrayediti ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: after making one large vessel of magnetic iron, one should attach two rings inside it, below, on the two sides. Having also made another small vessel of the same kind, one should fasten it to the rings in the large vessel in such a way that its bottom does not touch. Into that one should put swooned mercury, and fill the large vessel with sour gruel.

children.text: rase ṣāḍguṇyakārakaṃ ṣāḍguṇyaṃ vidyā vitarko vijñānaṃ smṛtistatparatā kriyā ityuktaṣaḍguṇapradaśaktijanakam evaṃvidharasopayoktā uktaṣāḍguṇyasiddhiṃ labhate ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Producing sixfold excellence in mercury" means generating the power that bestows the six qualities stated as learning, reasoning, knowledge, memory, intent application, and action. The meaning is that one who uses mercury of this kind obtains the accomplishment of the said sixfold excellence.
He states the transverse-distillation apparatus with the word beginning "one should put."

children.text: dīrghanatādhonālasaṃyute dīrghākāraṃ nataṃ nimnābhimukhaṃ ca yat adhonālaṃ tena saṃyute ||
children.translated_text: "Joined with a long, bent, downward tube" means joined with a downward tube that is long in form, bent, and directed downward.

children.text: ayaṃ vidhiḥ ekasmin ghaṭe rasaṃ nidhāya tasya udarādho dīrgham adholambitaṃ nālamekaṃ saṃyojya dvitīyaghaṭodarasthacchidre nālāgraṃ praveśya mṛdvastreṇa sandhimālipya ca ghaṭayormukham api tathā limpet rasakumbhādhaśca tīvrāgniṃ prajvālayet dvitīyaghaṭe svāduśītalaṃ jalaṃ ca prakṣipet iti ||
children.translated_text: This is the procedure: after placing mercury in one jar, one should attach to the lower belly of it a long tube hanging downward, insert the tip of the tube into a hole in the belly of a second jar, smear the joint with clay and cloth, and likewise seal the mouths of the two jars. Beneath the mercury-jar one should kindle a strong fire, and into the second jar one should put sweet, cold water.
He states the cup-apparatus with the word "cup."

children.text: vinatam agraṃ yasya tat nyubjīkṛtāgrabhāgam ūrdhvam uccaiḥkṛtaṃ daṇḍaṃ yasya tad unnatadaṇḍaṃ vinatāgraṃ ca tad ūrdhvadaṇḍaṃ ceti vinatāgrordhvadaṇḍakaṃ lauhaṃ lohamayaṃ vartulaṃ golākāraṃ caṣakaṃ kaṭorikā kāryamiti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That whose front is bent, that is, whose front part is turned downward, and whose handle is raised high upward, is called "having a raised handle and a bent front." The completion is: one should make an iron cup, made of metal and round in shape, a small bowl.
Although the word <s>caṣaka</s> means a drinking vessel for liquor, it has already been shown that it can mean simply a vessel.
"For the sake of <s>balijāraṇa</s>" means for the digestion of sulfur.
He states the jar-apparatus with the word beginning "four."
The conclusion is that a jar capable of holding water measuring sixteen dishes, and furnished with a mouth four finger-breadths wide, is the jar-apparatus.
<s>Āpyāyanaka</s> means the satiation of mercury and the like, that is, the production of sixfold excellence.

children.text: āpyāyanakam ityatra utthāpanakam iti pāṭhe rasotthāpanasādhanamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the reading here is <s>utthāpanaka</s> instead of <s>āpyāyanaka</s>, the meaning is "a means for raising mercury."
He states the brick-apparatus with the word beginning "having made."
<s>Malla</s> means an earthen dish-vessel.
<s>Pālikā</s> means a surrounding rim.

children.text: golākāraṃ gartamekam kṛtvā tatra śarāvaṃ saṃsthāpya tadupari madhyacchidrāmiṣṭakām ekāṃ vinyaset iṣṭakāgartaṃ paritaḥ aṅgulimitonnatam ālavālam ekaṃ ca kuryāt tata iṣṭakārandhre pāradaṃ vinikṣipya randhramukhe vastraṃ tadupari gandhakaṃ ca vinyasya śarāvāntareṇa ruddhvā śarāvālavālayoḥ saṃdhiṃ mṛdā samyagālipya ca vanyakarīṣaiḥ kapotākhyapuṭaṃ dadyāditi niṣkarṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The conclusion is this: after making one round pit, one should place a dish there; above it one should set a brick with a hole in the middle. Around the brick-pit one should also make a surrounding rim one finger high. Then, through the hole in the brick, one should put mercury; at the mouth of the hole one should place cloth, and above that sulfur. Having closed it with another dish, and having thoroughly smeared the joint between the dish and the rim with clay, one should apply a pigeon-named heating with wild dung-cakes.
He states the <s>vidyādhara</s> apparatus for extracting from cinnabar with the words beginning "above a pot."
At the word "pot," the understood addition is "facing upward."

children.text: atra hiṅgulākṛṣṭiprakārasya anuktatvāt granthāntaroktastatprakāraḥ pradarśyate tadyathā jambīrādirasaśodhitahiṅgulam adhaḥsthālyāṃ parṇopari saṃsthāpya kaṭhinīghṛṣṭatalabhāgām uttānāṃ sthālīmaparāṃ tadupari dattvā mṛdambarādibhiḥ saṃdhim ālipya ca adho jvālā deyā ūrdhvasthālyāṃ jalaṃ ca uṣṇe ca tasmin tat nikṣipya punardeyam evaṃ triṃśadvāraṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Since the method for extracting from cinnabar is not stated here, that method as stated in another treatise is now shown. It is as follows: cinnabar purified with the juice of citron and the like is placed on leaves in the lower pot. Another pot, turned upward and with its bottom part rubbed hard, is put above it. The joint is smeared with clay, cloth, and the like, and fire is applied below. Water is put into the upper pot, and when it becomes hot, that water is removed and fresh water is again added. One should do this thirty times.
In another treatise this has another name, <s>ūrdhvapātana</s> (upward distillation).
Some, immediately after this,
"Having filled a large vessel with sour gruels and with swooned mercury,
one should heat it for two yāmas for the purpose of raising the mercury."
Such an additional reading is found.
He states the navel-apparatus with the words beginning "in the middle of the dish."
<s>Kuḍya</s> means a wall, that is, something in the form of a surrounding rim.

children.text: atrocyamānayā atra yantre ucyamānayā kathyamānayā toyamṛdā lehavad ityādinā vakṣyamāṇayā paribhāṣikamṛdā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "By that which is being stated here" means by the technical clay being described in this apparatus, the clay to be mentioned below in the passage beginning "like paste with water and clay."

children.text: atra prathamaṃ samyag ācchādayed dvitīyaṃ samyak ruddhvā tṛtīyaṃ samyag ucyamānayā sambadhyate ||
children.translated_text: Here, first, "one should cover thoroughly" is connected with the second; "having sealed thoroughly" is connected with the third; and "with that which is being stated" is connected with "thoroughly."
He states the method for water-clay with the word beginning "like paste."
In the course of the present discussion of clay for smearing, he states the method for fire-clay with the word beginning "chalk."

children.text: ayaṃ vidhiḥ pātramadhye kiṃcid gartaṃ kṛtvā tatra rasagandhau niveśya gartasya caturdikṣu aṅgulocchrāyam ālavālaṃ kuryāt tato gostanākṛtimūṣayā sālavālaṃ sarasagandhakaṃ gartam ācchādya toyamṛdā sandhiṃ limpet tatastatra jalaṃ dattvā yantrādho vahniṃ dāpayed iti ||
children.translated_text: This is the procedure: after making a small pit in the middle of the vessel, one should place mercury and sulfur there. Around the pit on the four sides one should make a surrounding rim one finger high. Then, with a crucible shaped like a cow's udder, one should cover the rimmed pit containing mercury and sulfur, smear the joint with water-clay, then put water there and have fire applied beneath the apparatus.
He states the swallowed-apparatus with the word "crucible."
"For cooking the lord of mercury" means for cooking mercury.
He states the fumigation-apparatus with the word beginning "having made."
"At the neck-support" means at a particular support, like a small bowl at the neck-region, for placing rods.

children.text: atra prathamaṃ tiryak lohaśalākā ityanena dvitīyaṃ ca vinikṣipet ityanena sambadhyate ||
children.translated_text: Here, first, the phrase "iron rods crosswise" is connected with the second instruction, "one should insert."

children.text: tiryak vakrākārāḥ tanvīḥ sūkṣmāḥ lohaśalākāḥ tiryak vakrabhāvena vinikṣipet ityanvayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The construction is: one should insert thin, fine iron rods crosswise, that is, in a bent, transverse form.
Now, "by that," and so on.

children.text: uktavidhinā hatāni kṛtsnāni patrāṇi drutaṃ garbhe dravanti tataśca rasaḥ sa svarṇapatradravaḥ vegena carati svakāryaṃ sādhayatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that all the leaves struck in the prescribed manner quickly melt in the interior; then the mercury, namely the molten gold leaves, moves rapidly, accomplishing its own operation.
It has been said, "one should place smoke below the leaves." What is that smoke? He states this with the word beginning "sulfur."
"First" means best.

children.text: dairghyavistārato 'ṣṭāṅgulamānaṃ lohapātramekaṃ kārayitvā tasya kaṇṭhādhaḥ aṅgulidvayaparimitasthāne galādhāre sūkṣmatiryaglohaśalākāḥ tiryagbhāvena vinyasya tadupari kaṇṭakavedhyasvarṇapatrāṇi sthāpayet tatpatrādhaḥ pātrābhyantare gandhakaharitālamanaḥśilābhiḥ kṛtakajjalīṃ mṛtanāgaṃ vā nikṣipya adhomukhapātrāntareṇa tat pātraṃ pidhāya mṛdādinā sandhiṃ ruddhvā ca pātrādho vahniṃ prajvālayettena saṃtaptakajjalyādito dhūmaṃ nirgatya svarṇapatre lagiṣyati patrāṇi tāni bhasmībhavanti garbhe dravanti ca ||
