children.translated_text: After having made a single iron vessel measuring eight fingers in length and breadth, one should place fine transverse iron rods crosswise at the neck-support, at a place two fingers below its neck. Above them one should place gold leaves pierced by thorns. Below those leaves, inside the vessel, one should put either a collyrium-like mixture made from sulfur, orpiment, and realgar, or dead lead. Then one should cover that vessel with another vessel facing downward, seal the joint with clay and the like, and kindle fire below the vessel. By this, smoke will come forth from the heated collyrium-like mixture and the rest, and will adhere to the gold leaves. Those leaves become ash and melt in the interior.
This is clear.

children.text: svedanīyantratayā prāguktamapi idaṃ saṃjñāntarapradarśanārthaṃ punaruktam athavā tatra sthālyā viśeṣo noktaḥ ataḥ yā kācit sthālī eva grāhyā atra tu sthūlasthālī eva grāhyā ataḥ svedanīyantrāt asya vaiśiṣṭyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Although this has already been stated as a steaming apparatus, it is repeated here in order to show another technical name. Or else, there the particular kind of pot was not stated, so any pot whatsoever was to be taken; here, however, only a thick pot is to be taken. Therefore this is its distinction from the steaming apparatus.
He explains the mortar-apparatus with the word beginning "suitable for a mortar."
"Raised" means elevated at the side.

children.text: dīrghaḥ āyāmena unnataḥ iti dīrghotsedhayor bhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Long" means elevated in length; thus there is a difference between length and height.

children.text: gharṣaṇī kaṇḍanī putrikā iti yāvat noﾡā iti bhāṣā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gharṣaṇī</s>, <s>kaṇḍanī</s>, and <s>putrikā</s> mean much the same thing; in the vernacular, it is called noā.
<s>Gharṣa</s> means the stone pestle.
For grinding, he states a second, round mortar with the word beginning "twelve."
"The grinder," and so on.

children.text: putrikā adhobhāge cipiṭavadvistīrṇā uparibhāge ca sukhena yathā dhāraṇīyā bhavati tathā kartavyā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that the pestle should be made broad like a flattened object at its lower part, and at its upper part in such a way that it can be held comfortably.
He states the excellent clay for a crucible with the word beginning "clay."
"White and coarse" means white in color and also coarse.

children.text: athavā śoṇapāṇḍurā raktapāṇḍumiśravarṇā cirādhmānasahā dīrghakālaṃ vyāpya agnisaṃtāpaṃ prāpyāpi avidāraṇaśīlā evaṃvidhā yā śarkarā mṛttikā kaṅkararūpā mṛttikā ||
children.translated_text: Or else, it is red-white, that is, of a color mixed of red and white; it withstands long heating, meaning that even after undergoing the heat of fire for a long time, it does not split. Such gravelly clay is clay in the form of small stones.
In the absence of gravelly clay, he states the clay to be taken with the word beginning "that."

children.text: vālmīkī kṛmiśailodbhavā mṛd uimāṭī iti vaṅgabhāṣā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vālmīkī</s> is earth produced from an anthill; in Bengali it is called uimāṭī.
<s>Kaulālī</s> means potter's clay.
<s>Hayaladdi</s> means horse dung.
He states the other ingredients with the words beginning "white stones."
"White stones" means white rocks.
<s>Kharpara</s> is a fragment of a potsherd, that is, burnt clay.

children.text: śaṇakharpare ityatra śaṇakarpaṭe iti pāṭhe karpaṭaṃ chinnavastram ||
children.translated_text: Where the text reads <s>śaṇakharpare</s>, if the reading is <s>śaṇakarpaṭe</s>, then <s>karpaṭa</s> means a torn cloth.
<s>Laddi</s> means horse dung.
<s>Kiṭṭa</s> means iron slag.
<s>Kṛṣṇamṛtsnā</s> is black-colored clay.
"With crucible clay" means together with clay suitable for making a crucible.
He explains the <s>vajramūṣā</s> with the word beginning "of clay."
"Of clay" means of clay of the kind previously stated.
"Two parts of hemp and dung" means two parts each of hemp and dung.
"Having broken up" means having pulverized.
He explains the <s>yogamūṣā</s> with the word beginning "burnt."
Here the word "burnt" is connected separately with charcoal and husks.
<s>Mṛtsnā</s> means gravelly clay endowed with qualities such as whiteness and coarseness.
"Combined with the respective <s>viḍa</s>" means mixed with the <s>viḍa</s> previously described for digesting mercury.
"Smeared with the respective <s>viḍa</s>" means coated with that same <s>viḍa</s>.

children.text: dagdhāṅgārādiviḍāntaṃ sarvamekatra saṃnīya mūṣāṃ viracayya viḍena liptvā śuṣkīkṛtya gṛhṇīyāditi ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that one should bring together everything from burnt charcoal through <s>viḍa</s>, make a crucible, smear it with <s>viḍa</s>, dry it, and then use it.
He explains the crucible useful for melting diamond with the word beginning "furnace clay."

children.text: gāraśabdo'tra koṣṭhāgārikārthakaḥ nāmaikadeśenāpi nāmasākalyagrahaṇam iti nyāyāt koṣṭhāgārikā mṛttikāviśeṣaḥ kumīre pokāra moṭī iti bhāṣā ||
children.translated_text: Here the word <s>gāra</s> denotes <s>koṣṭhāgārikā</s>. According to the rule that even by part of a name the whole name is understood, <s>koṣṭhāgārikā</s> is a particular kind of clay; in the vernacular it is called kumīre pokāra moṭī.

children.text: bhūnāgaśabdenāpi tanmṛttikā grāhyā evaṃ ca gārabhūnāgadhautābhyāṃ dhautakoṣṭhāgārikākiñculūkamṛdbhyām ||
children.translated_text: By the word <s>bhūnāga</s> too, that same clay is to be understood. Thus, by <s>gāra</s>, <s>bhūnāga</s>, and <s>dhautā</s>, washed <s>koṣṭhāgārikā</s> and earth from the <s>kiñculūka</s> are meant.
"Crucible clay" is any one among the previously stated gravelly, anthill, potter's, and other clays.

children.text: gārādituṣāntaṃ sarvaṃ samam mṛttikā ca sarvaiḥ samānā grāhyā ||
children.translated_text: Everything from <s>gāra</s> through husks is equal, and the clay too should be taken equal to all of them.
"<s>Krauñcikā</s>," and so on.

children.text: yantramātre hi krauñcikā saṃjñā vartate sā hi bahudhā vividhaprakārā ityanvayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The construction is: the name <s>krauñcikā</s> applies to apparatus in general, and it is of many diverse kinds.
He explains the <s>gāramūṣā</s> with the word beginning "milk."

children.text: gārasya ṣaḍguṇatvaṃ kiṭṭāṅgāraśaṇānāṃ ca pratyekam aṣṭaguṇatvaṃ kṛṣṇamṛdapekṣayā bodhyam ||
children.translated_text: It should be understood that the sixfold quantity of <s>gāra</s>, and the eightfold quantities of slag, charcoal, and hemp respectively, are relative to the black clay.
The milk should be suitable for grinding.
He explains the excellent crucible with the word beginning "diamond."

children.text: vajraṃ tadākhyalauhaṃ pūrvoktasaṃgatyā tatkiṭṭaṃ vā bodhyam ||
children.translated_text: "Diamond" means the metal called by that name; or, because of the preceding context, its slag should be understood.
He explains the color-crucible with the word beginning "free from stones."
"Red" means red in color.
It has been prepared with the red group, that is, impregnated or boiled with a decoction of the group ending with mākṣika, beginning with kusumbha, which will be stated below.

children.text: kṣitikhecaralepitā kṣitiśca khaṃ ca kṣitikhe tatra carataḥ iti kṣitikhecarau bhūnāgamṛt kāśīśaṃ ca yadvā kṣitisthaḥ khecaraḥ kāśīśamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Smeared with earth-moving and sky-moving substances": earth and sky are "earth-sky"; those that move there are the earth-mover and sky-mover, namely bhūnāga clay and kāśīśa. Or else, the meaning is that kāśīśa is a sky-mover situated on the earth.
"For excellence of color" means for producing an excellent color, with the intention of generating a red color.
He explains the flux-crucible with the word beginning "that particular."
"Produced from the clay of that particular kind" means made from any one among the clays such as gravel and the like.

children.text: tattadbhedamṛdodbhūtā ityatra tattadviḍamṛdodbhūtā iti pāṭhe pūrvoktaviḍena pūrvoktamṛdā ca udbhūtā nirmitā ||
children.translated_text: Where the reading is "produced from the clay of that particular kind of flux," the meaning is: produced, that is, made, from the previously stated flux and the previously stated clay.

children.text: dehalohārthayogārthaṃ dehasya lauhavad dārḍhyasampādanārthā ye yogāḥ tadarthaṃ tatkarmasampādanārtham ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "For the sake of practices concerning the body and metal" means for those preparations that bring about firmness of the body like metal; that is, for carrying out that operation.
He explains another form of the crucible useful for melting the previously mentioned diamond with the word beginning "gāra."

children.text: matkuṇaḥ chārapokā iti khyātaḥ krimiviśeṣaḥ tasya śoṇitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Matkuṇa</s> is a particular insect known in the vernacular as <s>chārapokā</s>; with its blood.

children.text: abdadhvaniḥ vanataṇḍulīyakaḥ kāṃṭānaṭe iti bhāṣā bālābdadhvanimūlaiḥ navotpannataṇḍulīyamūlaiḥ yadvā vālaḥ aśvapucchakeśaḥ tathā abdadhvanimūlaṃ taiḥ liptā ityanenānvayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Abdadhvani</s> is the wild taṇḍulīyaka, called <s>kāṃṭānaṭe</s> in the vernacular. "With young abdadhvani roots" means with the newly grown roots of taṇḍulīya. Or else, <s>vāla</s> means the hair of a horse's tail; thus the construction is "smeared with those and with abdadhvani root."

children.text: draveṇa vyādhitā viddhā spṛṣṭā ityarthaḥ dravapūrṇā ityāśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Pierced by liquid" means penetrated or touched by liquid; the intention is that it is filled with liquid.
He explains the satiating of a crucible with the word beginning "when liquid."

children.text: dhmāyate aneneti dhmānamagniḥ tadyogataḥ agnisaṃyogād drave drāvaṇopayogini dravye dravībhāvamukhe dravībhavitum ārabdhe mūṣāyā yat kṣaṇam uddharaṇam agnitaḥ uttolanam avatāraṇamityarthaḥ tad āpyāyanaṃ tarpaṇaṃ sthāyitvasampādanam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That by which one blows is <s>dhmāna</s>, namely fire. Through its conjunction, that is, through contact with fire, when the liquid, the substance useful for melting, has reached the point of liquefaction and has begun to become liquid, the momentary lifting of the crucible, that is, raising it from the fire or taking it down, is called <s>āpyāyana</s>, satiation; the meaning is the production of durability.
He explains the brinjal-shaped crucible with the word beginning "brinjal."

children.text: vṛntākaṃ vārttākuḥ vārttākuphalasadṛśākārāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvā tatra dvādaśāṅguladīrghaṃ nālaṃ yojayet nālāgrabhāgaṃ ca dhustūrapuṣpavad uparyadho yugmarūpāvasthitam aṣṭāṅgulaṃ sacchidraṃ ca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛntāka</s> means brinjal. Having made a crucible shaped like the fruit of a brinjal, one should attach to it a tube twelve fingers long. The tip of the tube should be made like a dhattūra flower, arranged as a pair above and below, eight fingers long and furnished with holes.
He explains the baked crucible with the word beginning "potter."

children.text: ghaṭakapālayoḥ pṛthak pṛthak nirmāṇārthaṃ yaḥ pratirūpaḥ saḥ kulālabhāṇḍaśabdenocyate tadrūpā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The model used for separately making potsherds and cups is denoted by the expression "potter's vessel"; the meaning is that it has that form.
"For cooking pellets and the like" means for cooking pellets containing jewels and so forth.
He explains the spherical crucible with the word beginning "without a mouth."
The meaning is that it is spherical in shape and lacks an opening.
"Restraining the essence and the liquid" means preventing the outflow of liquid substances.
A spherical crucible, with the substances to be heated placed in the middle and its mouth properly closed, should be understood as a <s>golamūṣā</s>.
He explains the great crucible with the word beginning "at the bottom."

children.text: kūrparākārā kūrparaḥ kaphoṇiḥ bhujamadhyasandhir ityarthaḥ tadākārā ||
children.translated_text: "Elbow-shaped": <s>kūrpara</s> means the elbow, that is, the joint in the middle of the arm; it has that shape.
He explains the frog-crucible with the word beginning "frog."
<s>Maṇḍūka</s> means a frog; it has that shape.
"Measuring six fingers in depth, length, and breadth" means furnished with a depth, length, and breadth each measuring six fingers.
He explains the pestle-crucible with the word beginning "crucible."
It should be understood as round upward from the base.
"In cakribaddha mercury" refers to a particular medicine mentioned in the section on women's diseases.
He explains the characteristics of the charcoal furnace with the word beginning "royal cubit."
"Rising to a royal cubit" means two cubits high.
The detailed explanation of the royal cubit is to be seen in the explanation of the elephant-heating pit.
"Quadrangular" means four-cornered.
"Endowed with the breadth of a span" means twelve fingers wide.

children.text: dvāraṃ sārdhavitastyā ca ityasya dehalyadhaḥ ityanena saṃbandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "And the door is one and a half spans" is connected with the phrase "below the threshold."
<s>Dehalī</s>, the threshold, is the platform or sill at the lower part of the door.

children.text: prādeśapramitā aṅguṣṭhasya pradeśinyā vyāsaḥ prādeśa ucyate ityuktalakṣaṇā tarjanīsahitavistṛtāṅguṣṭhapramāṇā ||
children.translated_text: "Measuring a <s>prādeśa</s>": the distance between the thumb and the index finger is called a <s>prādeśa</s>. Thus it is of the measure defined as the outstretched thumb together with the index finger.
"Of the upper beam" means of the wooden piece situated above the door.

children.text: hastadvayotsedhaṃ hastamitāyāmavistāraṃ catuṣkoṇaṃ samantāt mṛnmayabhittiveṣṭitaṃ ca cullyākāramekaṃ mārttikaṃ yantraṃ kṛtvā tasya ekabhittau vitastivistaraṃ dvāraṃ dvārapiṇḍikādhaḥ aṣṭādaśāṅgulamānaṃ dvārāntaraṃ ca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: after making a single earthen apparatus in the form of a hearth, two cubits high, a cubit in length and breadth, quadrangular, and surrounded on all sides with clay walls, one should make in one of its walls a door one span wide, and below the door-sill another opening measuring eighteen fingers.

children.text: dvārordhvabhāge aṅguṣṭhatarjanyor madhyavat vistṛtāṃ bhittiṃ sthāpayitvā tadupari tadvadvistṛtaṃ dvāramanyat vidadhyāt tataḥ iṣṭakayā dvārasandhiṃ ruddhvā ālipya ca koṣṭhīmaṅgāraiḥ paripūrya dvābhyāṃ bhastrābhyāṃ dhamet ||
children.translated_text: In the part above the door one should set a wall as wide as the space between the thumb and index finger, and above that make another door of the same width. Then, after blocking the door-joint with a brick and smearing it, one should fill the furnace with charcoal and blow it with two bellows.

children.text: bhasmībhūte ca aṅgāre punarapi aṅgāraṃ sattvapātanagolādikaṃ ca pañca pañca kṛtvā ūrdhvadvāreṇa punaḥ punaḥ nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: When the charcoal has become ash, one should again and again put in more charcoal and balls for extraction of essence and the like, five at a time, through the upper door.

children.text: iyam aṅgārakoṣṭhī kharadravyāṇāṃ sattvapātane śubhā jñeyā ||
children.translated_text: This charcoal furnace should be known as excellent for extracting the essence of hard substances.
He explains the subterranean furnace with the word beginning "on firm ground."

children.text: kaṭhinamṛttikāyāṃ vitastimānaṃ vartulaṃ gartam ekaṃ kṛtvā tanmadhye caturaṅgulavistāraṃ caturaṅgulagabhīraṃ gartād bhūpṛṣṭhaparyantayāyivakrākṛtinālasaṃyuktam īṣaducchritaṃ ca gartamanyaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: In hard clay ground, after making one round pit of a span's measure, one should make in its middle another pit, four fingers wide and four fingers deep, furnished with a slightly raised, curved tube going from the pit up to the surface of the ground.

children.text: tataḥ abhyantaragartamadhye pañcarandhrasaṃyuktāṃ mṛccakrīṃ sthāpayitvā aṅgāraiḥ koṣṭhīṃ paripūrya ca ekabhastrayā pradhamet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after placing inside the inner pit a clay disk furnished with five holes, and after filling the furnace with charcoal, one should blow with a single bellows.

children.text: mṛdudravyāṇāṃ sattvapātanārtham iyaṃ pātālakoṣṭhīti jñeyamiti niṣkarṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The conclusion is that this is to be known as the <s>pātālakoṣṭhī</s> (subterranean furnace) for extracting the essence of soft substances.
He states the <s>gārakoṣṭhī</s> with the word beginning "twelve."

children.text: dvādaśāṅgulagabhīrā prādeśapramāṇavistāraviśiṣṭā koṣṭhī ekā kāryā tasyā ūrdhvaṃ caturaṅgule valayākāram ālavālam ekaṃ dattvā tadupari bahucchidrāṃ cakrīṃ nidhāya aṅgāraṃ nikṣipya ca vaṅkanālena pradhamet iti ||
children.translated_text: One should make a furnace twelve fingers deep and distinguished by a width measuring one span. Above it, at four fingers' height, one should set one circular basin; upon that, having placed a disk with many holes and deposited charcoal, one should blow through a bent tube.
"Destroyer of polished metal" means one that kills purified iron.

children.text: gārakoṣṭhikāyāṃ vaṅkanālam ityuktaṃ kiṃ tat vaṅkanālam ityāśaṃsāyāmāha mūṣāmṛdbhiriti ||
children.translated_text: Since a bent tube is mentioned in connection with the small <s>gārakoṣṭhī</s>, in anticipation of the question, "What is that bent tube?" he says, "with crucible-clays."

children.text: śarkarādīnām anyatamābhiḥ mūṣopayogimṛdbhiḥ aratnipramitaṃ dṛḍhaṃ nālaṃ kṛtvā tanmukhe pañcāṅgulapramāṇam adhomukhaṃ nālam ekaṃ yojayet dṛḍhadhmānāya tad vaṅkanālaṃ veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: Having made a firm tube, one cubit in measure, from one among gravel and the other clays used for crucibles, one should attach at its mouth a downward-facing tube five fingers in measure. That should be understood as the bent tube for firm blowing.
He states the <s>kukkuṭapuṭa</s> (cock-shaped heating) with the word "heating."
"Two spans high" means one cubit high.
And just that broad at the bottom, that is, one cubit wide in the lower part as well.

children.text: etattu bhūmerupari eva kāryaṃ na tu gartaṃ khanitvā ||
children.translated_text: But this should be made only on top of the ground, not by digging a pit.
"Having bound" means having enclosed it in a crucible and sealed it.
For making the ash of mercury and orpiment, for making the ash of mercury, and for making copper ash.

children.text: vahnimitrāḥ mūṣāḥ dīrghakālaṃ vahninā sahāvasthānāt asyā vahnimitratvaṃ jñātavyam ||
children.translated_text: "Friends of fire" are crucibles; because they remain together with fire for a long time, their friendship with fire should be understood.
The rest is clear.
<s>Tumbinī</s> is bitter gourd, or else pine wood.
<s>Amlīka</s> is tamarind fruit.
<s>Rasapattrikā</s> is the sour juice of wood-apple.
<s>Nīlaka</s> is marking-nut.

children.text: uttamakaṇṭikā eraṇḍaviśeṣaḥ vāgā bhereṇḍā jāmālagoṭā iti ca bhāṣā yadvā uttamakaṇṭikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Uttamakaṇṭikā</s> is a variety of castor, called in the vernacular <s>vāgā</s>, <s>bhereṇḍā</s>, and <s>jāmālagoṭā</s>; or else it is simply <s>uttamakaṇṭikā</s>.
<s>Karpūragandhinī</s> is a variety of turmeric with the fragrance of camphor.

children.text: kācaḥ mṛttikāviśeṣaḥ sa ca kṣārarasaḥ uṣṇavīryaḥ añjanāddṛṣṭikārakaḥ viḍākhyalavaṇo vā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāca</s> is a particular kind of clay; it has an alkaline taste, hot potency, and, when applied as collyrium, benefits the sight. Or it is the salt called <s>viḍa</s>.
<s>Śiprā</s> means a particular kind of shell.

children.text: parpaṭyādi sapta kañcukānāṃ saṃjñāḥ tatra parpaṭīsadṛśaśoṣakatvāt parpaṭī parpaṭī yathā śoṣiṇī grāhiṇī ca pāradasya parpaṭyākhyakañcuko'pi naradehe tatkriyājananī vidārakatvāt pāṭanī malabhedakatvād bhedinī śārīradhātūnāṃ dravatvasaṃpādanād drāvī doṣavardhakatvāt malakarī andhatvajananād andhakārī dhvāṅkṣo yathā karkaśasvaro bhavati tathā svarapāruṣyajananād dhvāṅkṣīti jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Parpaṭī</s> and the others are the seven names of the sheaths. Among them, because it dries like <s>parpaṭī</s>, it is <s>parpaṭī</s>; just as <s>parpaṭī</s> is drying and absorbent, so the sheath of mercury called <s>parpaṭī</s> produces that action in the human body. Because it splits, it is <s>pāṭanī</s>; because it breaks up impurity, it is <s>bhedinī</s>; because it brings about fluidity in the bodily constituents, it is <s>drāvī</s>; because it increases the doṣas, it is <s>malakarī</s>; because it causes blindness, it is <s>andhakārī</s>; and because, just as a crow is harsh-voiced, it produces roughness of the voice, it should be known as <s>dhvāṅkṣī</s>.
<s>Śampāka</s> is <s>āragvadha</s>.
He states <s>ābhāsabandha</s> (semblance-binding) with the word beginning "heated in a puṭa."

children.text: dhātumūlādyaiḥ prāguktasvarṇādidhātubhistathā sarpākṣyādimūlikābhiḥ bhāvitaḥ puṭitaśca rasaḥ guṇavaikṛteḥ dravyāntarasaṃyogena svābhāvikaguṇaviparyayāt svabhāvatāṃ svābhāvikaguṇādikaṃ muktvā yogaṃ yogavāhitāṃ yāti sa ābhāsaḥ kathyate iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Mercury that has been impregnated and heated in a <s>puṭa</s> with metals and roots, that is, with the previously mentioned metals such as gold and with herbs such as <s>sarpākṣī</s>, through alteration of its qualities, namely through the reversal of its natural qualities by combination with another substance, abandons its own nature, its natural qualities and so forth, and assumes <s>yogavāhitā</s> (the capacity to carry a formulation's effect). It is called <s>ābhāsa</s>; this is the supplied completion.
He states <s>kṣārabandha</s> (alkali-binding) with the word beginning "conch."
"Processed" means well prepared by trituration, heating in a <s>puṭa</s>, and the like.
The rest is clear.
He states <s>khoṭabandha</s> with the word "binding."
"<s>Khoṭatā</s>" means the nature of not flying away even when placed in fire, as has been said:
"When it remains in the midst of fire, that is the mark of what is bound as <s>khoṭa</s>,"
Thus.

children.text: dhmāto dhmātaḥ bhastrayā punaḥ punar ādhmāpita ityarthaḥ kṣayaṃ vrajet dravyāntareṇa saha ekībhāvāt adarśanatāṃ gacchedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Blown, blown" means repeatedly blown upon with a bellows. "It should undergo loss" means that, because of becoming one with another substance, it becomes invisible.

children.text: yogoktaphaladāyakaḥ yasmin yoge sa prayojyaḥ tasya phalautkarṣyaprada ityarthaḥ athavā svedanamardanārthaṃ gṛhītakalkadravyāṇām upayoge yat phalaṃ tatphalaprada ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Bestowing the fruit stated for the formulation" means that, in whatever formulation it is to be used, it gives excellence to that formulation's result. Or it means that it gives the result obtained from using the paste substances taken for steaming and trituration.
He states <s>kajjalībandha</s> (black-sulfide binding) with the word beginning "kajjalī."
"Very smooth" means glossy and unctuous.
"Joined with the respective formulation" means purified by combination with the substances that purify mercury and sulfur.
He states <s>nirjīvabandha</s> (lifeless binding) with the word beginning "digested mica."
"Digested mica" means mica that has been swallowed up.
"Completely digested sulfur" means sulfur that has been fully swallowed.
He explains the word beginning "all."

children.text: akhilānāṃ sarveṣāṃ lohānāṃ svarṇādīnāmityarthaḥ mauliḥ śirobhūṣaṇasvarūpaḥ sarvalohopayoge ye guṇā bhavanti tebhyo'pyadhikaguṇaprada ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Of all" means of all metals, such as gold. "Crest-jewel" means something in the form of a head ornament; the sense is that it grants qualities superior even to those that arise in the use of all metals.
Because it is incapable of escaping even when joined with fire, its lifelessness should be understood.
He states <s>śṛṅkhalābandha</s> (chain-binding) with the word beginning "diamond and so on."

children.text: vajrādinihataḥ hīrakādisahayogena māritaḥ sūtaḥ tadvā samaḥ samaparimitaḥ aparaśca hataḥ prakārāntareṇa māritaḥ sūtaḥ śṛṅkhalābaddhasūtaḥ ubhayor mardanād iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Struck by diamond and the like" means mercury killed by conjunction with diamond and similar substances; and another killed mercury, equal to that in quantity, means mercury killed by another method. It is <s>śṛṅkhalābaddhasūta</s> (chain-bound mercury), by the trituration of the two; this is the supplied completion.

children.text: citraprabhāvām alaukikasāmarthyāṃ vegena vyāptiṃ śṛṅkhalābandhasūtasya dehe iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Of wondrous power" means of extraordinary efficacy; the swift pervasion is in the body by chain-bound mercury, this is the supplied completion.
He states <s>drutibandha</s> (liquefaction-binding) with the word beginning "joined."

children.text: bāhyadrutibhiḥ rasasya dravatvasampādakakriyāviśeṣaiḥ yuktaḥ api bandhaṃ gataḥ bandhanatāṃ prāptaḥ vā athavā bhasitasvarūpaḥ bhasmībhūtaḥ sūtaḥ drutibaddhanāmā jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even when joined with external liquefactions, that is, with special operations that produce fluidity in mercury, mercury that has entered a binding, that is, has attained the state of being bound, or else has the form of ash, that is, has become ash, should be known by the name <s>drutibaddha</s>.

children.text: saḥ drutibaddhasūtaḥ rājikā rāī iti khyātaḥ raktavarṇasarṣapaviśeṣaḥ tasyāḥ pādamitaḥ caturthabhāgaparimitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>drutibaddha</s> mercury is one fourth of a <s>rājikā</s>, a particular red-colored mustard seed known as <s>rāī</s>.
He explains fire-binding with the word 'alone'.
'Alone' means not combined with another substance.
'Joined with a preparation' means combined with another substance.
'Blown' means heated in fire.

children.text: akṣīṇaḥ agnitāpe'pi yathāmātrāyāṃ sthitaḥ na tu kiṃcid apyūnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Undiminished' means remaining in its original measure even under the heat of fire, and not reduced at all.
'Producing sky-going and the like' means that, when held in the mouth, it grants the capacity for movement through the sky.

children.text: uddeśagranthe jalabandho'gnibandhaśca susaṃskṛtakṛtābhidhaḥ ityanena agnibandhānantaraṃ mahābandhācca prāk susaṃskṛtakṛtākhyabandhāntarasya samullekho vidyate vivaraṇagranthe tu tadullekhādarśanāt bandhaḥ saḥ lipikarapramādāt pramādāntarādvā adarśanatāṃ gata iti manye ||
children.translated_text: In the summary text, by the statement 'water-binding and fire-binding, and the one called well-processed-maker,' there is mention of another binding called <s>susaṃskṛtakṛt</s> after fire-binding and before great-binding. But in the explanatory text, since no mention of it is seen, I think that this binding has disappeared through a scribe's error or some other error.

children.text: kiṃca susaṃskṛtakṛtābhidhaḥ ityasya agnibandhasya viśeṣaṇatvamapi na yujyate tathātve bandhasya caturviṃśatisaṃkhyatvāt pañcaviṃśatisaṃkhyākān rasabandhān pracakṣmahe iti pratijñāhānyāpatteriti ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, it is also not proper to take 'called <s>susaṃskṛtakṛt</s>' as an adjective of fire-binding. For, if that were so, since the bindings would number twenty-four, there would follow the loss of the stated promise, 'we shall explain twenty-five mercury-bindings.'
'Compact' means not raised or depressed, that is, having all its parts even.

children.text: nirbandhaḥ yathāyatham asaṃpāditabandhanakriyaḥ cet kṣaṇāt dravati agnau iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is 'unbound,' that is, if the binding operation has not been properly accomplished, it melts in a moment; 'in fire' is to be supplied.
